publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Communication barriers between deaf individuals and hearing people can lead to several significant problems such as social integration, reduced access to information and reduced opportunities thereby affecting quality of life of deaf individuals. Use of sign language for communication serves as the primary means to address these challenges. However, understanding of the sign language is very difficult for hearing individuals. To address this issue, we present a Real-Time Sign Language to text and Speech Converter to facilitate effective communication between deaf and hearing individuals. This paper presents a novel approach to sign language recognition using OpenCV and MediaPipe. The main aim of the paper is to develop real time computer vision that can translate sign language gestures into text in real-time. We use image processing techniques to segment and analyze sign gestures, OpenCV to record and process these gestures, MediaPipe for hand tracking and gesture prediction and a text-to-speech engine to translate the text into speech for auditory communication. Thus, this study offers a comprehensive sign language to speech converter system that has the potential to significantly improve communication between the deaf community and the hearing people.

articleTitle: Enhancing Summarization of Legal Text Documents using Pre-trained Models
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: A very relevant challenge of summarizing legal text documents often exceeds the length, therefore being complex, was addressed using pre-trained models such as BART and PEGASUS. In the paper, the issue is discussed-the challenge that these pre-trained models face while being effective in general text summarization tasks, which becomes difficult in legal contexts due to specialized vocabulary and structure of legal documents. The authors fine-tune these models using the BillSum dataset-provided US Congressional bills as a proxy for court documents. Evaluation on ROUGE metrics reveals that BART outperforms PEGASUS in summation of content structures of legal texts to the greatest extent intended. The results suggest that the pre-trained models significantly improve the process of summarizing legal documents, both for professionals in law and general readers who would otherwise have to wade through an extensive amount of legal information.

articleTitle: An Improved Inception V3 Deep learning model for Cardiovascular Disease Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Accurate prediction of cardiovascular disease risk is essential for improving healthcare outcomes and resource management. This study uses a cardiovascular disease dataset and applies deep learning models to forecast disease risk in specific patient populations. In our approach, data preprocessing encompassed normalization and partitioning of the dataset into training and test subsets. We utilized the Inception V3 model, conducting training over ten epochs for data analysis. We also assessed alternative models to broaden our evaluation—specifically, VGG 16, VGG 19, ResNet 34, and ResNet 50. These models were analyzed based on essential performance metrics, such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score. Inception V3 achieved the highest accuracy at 98%, followed by VGG 16 at 86%, VGG 19 at 80%, ResNet 34 at 78%, and ResNet 50 at 68%. We further enhanced our analysis with visual tools such as histograms and heat maps to identify key trends and correlations in the data. These insights provided a clearer understanding of significant risk factors and potential prevention strategies. Our findings demonstrate that deep learning models, particularly Inception V3, are highly effective for cardiovascular disease prediction, contributing to improved healthcare strategies and decision-making.

articleTitle: Kidney Stone Prediction Based on Urine Analysis: A Comprehensive Study of Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Kidney stones, medically known as renal calculi, are solid crystal aggregations formed in the urinary tract, affecting millions globally. They are a common yet painful urological condition that can lead to severe health complications such as infections, urinary obstruction, and chronic kidney disease if not diagnosed and treated promptly. Identifying kidney stones early allows for more effective intervention strategies, minimizing patient discomfort and reducing healthcare costs. This paper explores a comprehensive evaluation of machine learning models for predicting kidney stone occurrence based on urine analysis. Using a dataset comprising 79 samples with six physical features such as specific gravity, pH, osmolarity, conductivity, urea concentration, and calcium concentration and ten machine learning models were evaluated: K-Nearest Neighbors, Support Vector Machine, Naive Bayes, Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Decision Tree, Adaboost, XGBoost, Gradient Boosting and Stacking. Logistic Regression achieved the highest accuracy of 0.93 with a precision of 0.87, demonstrating its suitability for such predictions. This research highlights the potential of ML based diagnostics in healthcare applications.

articleTitle: SVR: Feature Selection Based Support Vector Regression for Humidity Data Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Weather data like humidity is a key indicator in meteorology which is influenced by multiple climatic factors. Higher humidity levels become a threat to human health, cause storms and also lead to increase in rainfall, temperature and air borne pollutants. Therefore, prediction of humidity can be helpful in taking necessary action plans for protection of both human life and environment. Weather data can be predicted by multiple regression methods using explanatory variables. However, the effectiveness and prediction accuracy of the multiple regression methods are affected by the irrelevant or non-informative features and the uncertainties lie with the predictions. Feature selection (FS) methods can improve the effectiveness of prediction models and also reduce the uncertainties of predictions by reducing the dimensionality of the dataset by selecting more explanatory variables. On this basis, we have proposed feature selection-based support vector regression (SVR). The proposed hybrid model incorporates Random Forest (RF) model-based FS method in SVR to predict the future humidity data. Performance of RF model-based FS method is compared with two other feature selection methods like correlation-based method and recursive feature elimination (RFE) method. The prediction accuracy of the SVR model is compared with two other multiple regression models: artificial neural network (ANN) regression and decision tree regression (DTR).

articleTitle: Classification Algorithms for Pump Control as well as Multi-Objective Optimization for Pump Scheduling
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Over or undersupply of water will negatively impact crop health. A Smart Irrigation system is the need of the hour in agriculture technology which can optimize water use and enhance crop health for sustainable and precision farming promoting higher yields. IoT and AI-driven systems are more efficient than a simple automated system by reducing water and power wastage. Our system leverages IoT devices such as capacitive soil moisture sensors and DHT-11 sensors. Our system predicts pump activation status (binary classification: pump on/off) based on environmental features. It Optimizes water usage by accurately determining the necessary conditions for pump activation, thereby reducing over-irrigation and conserving resources. We used DNN with 3 layers with a feed-forward neural network. The result from Deep Neural Network shows an accuracy of 99% with an F1 score of 99.5% while a precision of 99.7% with a recall of 99.3% which predicts the optimal parameters for pump scheduling. Similarly, the LSTM model achieved 99.5% accuracy with an F1 score of 99.5% while precision is 99.6% and recall was 99.3% and the CNN model resulted with 86% accuracy and an F1 score of 84.4% with a precision of 97.4% and recall of 74.5%. Similarly, the RNN model resulted in 86% accuracy with an F1 score of 85% precision of 92%, and recall of 80% whereas the CNN + LSTM hybrid model resulted in 87% accuracy and an F1 score of 86.7% with 90.6% of precision and recall of 83%.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Machine Learning Models in Heart Stroke Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Stroke, a persistent medical condition with a rising yearly occurrence, can be triggered by the sudden interruption of blood flow to a section of the brain or heart. Early symptom detection can provide valuable information for prognosticating stroke and promoting healthy lifestyles. This research proposes guidelines for developing effective machine learning-based methods to identify heart stroke disorders. The study incorporates various ML techniques alongside key factors such as hypertension, BMI, cardiac disease, mean glucose levels, tobacco use, previous stroke incidents, and patient age. A comparative analysis and review of diverse machine learning techniques employed to predict heart stroke occurrence has been presented in the paper. A performance analysis of Gradient Boosting Classifier (GBC), AdaBoost Classifier, Support Vector Classifier (SVC), Random Forest Classifier (RFC), and Logistic Regression Classifier (LR) has been performed and the results have been evaluated using the confusion matrix followed by key findings.

articleTitle: Object Detection and Tracking for the Visually Impaired with YOLO 11
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: The latest advancements in AI and computer vision technology can grant artificial eyes to those who have not seen the world. With computer vision model YOLO 11, this is becoming a reality. This is a solution, which can empower blind people to "see" their surroundings through their ears. The people who are blind have had to depend heavily on others to carry out daily activities or simple tasks like traveling, reading, or counting currency are significant challenges. While it may not be possible to restore solution vision to everyone, we can use other senses to mitigate these difficulties. By using AI and computer vision, we are not just giving vision means sight to machines, but also providing enhanced sensory experiences like ears and a mouth. The same technology can provide eyes, ears, and even a mouth to humans who lack them. In this experiment we have taken small steps to aid those with visual impairments, enabling them to navigate their world with ease and confidence.Through this small experiment, blind people can detect approaching objects and respond accordingly. By utilizing a custom-trained model, the model can recognize familiar persons, surroundings, text (OCR), currency, and even obstacles like potholes on roads. The model can detect and track these nearby elements, generating text that is then converted into sound. Blind individuals can listen to this audio through earphones in real time and navigate their environment with greater independence and confidence.

articleTitle: Dynamic Time Slice Prediction in Round Robin CPU Scheduling using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Efficient CPU scheduling is crucial for optimizing system performance and resource utilization in multitasking operating systems. The Round Robin (RR) scheduling algorithm, known for its simplicity and fairness, often suffers from inefficiencies due to its use of a constant time slice, leading to increased waiting time (WT) and turnaround time (TAT) under varying workloads. This research addresses these limitations by proposing an optimized RR CPU scheduling algorithm that employs dynamic time slicing (DTS) using Artificial Neural Networks (ANN). DTS is adjusted based on CPU burst time (BT), with the aim of minimizing WT and TAT. Various regression techniques and ANN models are utilized to predict the DTS. These models are trained and evaluated using GWA-T-4 AuverGrid dataset of process attributes, with key performance metrics such as Mean Squared Error (MSE), R-squared (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>), average WT and average TAT used to assess their effectiveness. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed RR method, especially when optimized with ANN, significantly reduces WT and TAT compared to other RR methods.

articleTitle: Fast Underwater Scene Restoration for Non-Uniform Degradation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Deep learning-based underwater image restoration models achieve great performance when dealing with uniform artifacts in the image. However, most existing approaches primarily focus on distortion due to non-uniform illumination, neglecting the impact of non-homogeneous suspended particles in the water. This research introduces a system for fast underwater scene visibility enhancement using a deep multi-patch hierarchical neural network. The system aims to remove non-homogeneous artifacts in underwater environments in high speed. The proposed system is robust to different underwater environments with non-uniform artifacts. By improving the clarity of camera feeds in challenging underwater conditions, the system supports a wide range of underwater exploration applications.

articleTitle: Triplet Subnet-based Feature and Weight Selection Mechanism in Siamese Network for Kinship Verification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: This paper proposes a kinship verification approach that was derived from the Siamese network by introducing a Triplet subnet-based feature and weight selection (TS-FW) mechanism. The traditional Siamese network has two subnetworks with a weight-sharing mechanism during the training process. Each subnetworks have a sequence of convolutional filters and max-pooling layers for extracting the facial descriptors. Few convolutional filters are automatically trained to extract the global descriptors and other convolutional filters are used to extract the local descriptors. In order to specifically focus on global and local descriptors, the proposed approach uses three subnets in each subnetwork of the Siamese network. The subnets are named primary subnet, secondary-A, and secondary-B subnet. The primary subnet updates the weights based on the loss function, while the secondary subnets use the weights that are derived from the primary subnet. The secondary subnets use the feature map selected by the feature map selection process. The evaluation of the suggested kinship verification scheme was done using the accuracy scale with the datasets namely KinFaceW-I and TSKinFace dataset. In the case of the KinFaceW-I dataset the proposed TS-FW approach results in an average accuracy of 82.9%, 85.9%, 86.9%, and 91.9% in verifying M-S, F-S, F-D, and M-D kinship relations. The proposed scheme yields an average verification accuracy of 96.2% and 86.9% when evaluated using the TSkinFace and KinFaceW-I datasets respectively.

articleTitle: SPEAR: Sparse PCA-Enhanced Adaptive Resampling for Multi-class Imbalanced Data
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Resampling techniques like SMOTE and its variants are commonly used to address class imbalance in datasets. However, this method often generates non-representative samples that do not reflect the inherent structure of the dataset. This issue is particularly pronounced in sparse multi-class imbalanced datasets, where resampling can lead to improper data patterns and degrade the performance of models trained on such data. To address these limitations, a novel Sparse PCA-Enhanced Adaptive Resampling (SPEAR) is proposed and tailored for sparse imbalanced datasets. The method modifies class distributions by calculating the average class size, down-sampling larger classes through k-Means, and up-sampling smaller ones using Sparse Principal Component Analysis (SPCA) before integrating the resampled data back into the original distributions. Sparse PCA encourages sparsity in the principal components, preserving the data structure and resembling the original data patterns. The proposed approach was evaluated on ten datasets, comparing its performance against eight baseline resampling methods using three classifiers. Experimental results demonstrate that the method consistently outperforms the baselines, achieving higher G-mean values on average. Statistical tests further confirm the significance of these improvements, underscoring the efficacy of the proposed technique in addressing class imbalance, particularly in sparse datasets.

articleTitle: Teach me : AI-Powered Voice Chat Robot Using Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: This paper presents TEACH ME: An Artificial Intelligence-Powered Voice Chat Robot Integrated with the Internet of Things (IoT), designed to facilitate flexible, voice-powered communication with connected devices Leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs). TEACH ME Natural Language Processing Increases (NLP) Powerful, robust robotic voice translation enables them to create, engage in active conversations, and respond in human-like ways that integrate LLMs with the IoT extend beyond traditional systems for experiencing it is highly personalized and contextual, and allows users to interact with smart devices This system design seamlessly combines the capabilities of LLMs with IoT devices, 1999—creating new opportunities for applications in areas such as smart home automation, education, customer support, etc. TEACH ME’s key components include real-time voice recognition, advanced response generation, and IoT-powered task performance. Examines applicability and future directions.

articleTitle: Quadrant Analysis of Learner’s Performance in Quantitative Aptitude and Coding
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: With the aim of improving learning for varied learners in various situations, abstract educational data mining (EDM) entails utilising methodologies, tools, and research to extract significant insights from educational data repositories. The primary objective of this research is to examine the quantitative aptitude and coding performance of 366 engineering undergraduate students. A convenience and random sampling technique was used to gather the dataset, and preprocessing was then performed to guarantee data completeness. Descriptive statistics demonstrate that students do well overall in both areas, with slightly more variability in Quantitative Aptitude scores than in Coding, where performance is more constant. Based on how well the students performed in these two areas, a quadrant analysis was used to classify the students into four groups: Excellent, Good, Average, and Poor. The results of this analysis demonstrated the differences in the way students developed in the two skill areas, highlighting the significance of tailored educational interventions. Quantitative aptitude and coding had a weakly positive link, according to the correlation study, indicating that these abilities are largely independent of one another. The study highlights that in order to help pupils in these areas, specific instructional practices are required. It is advised to connect technology with pedagogy through the Metacognition-aided Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) framework. This will improve student outcomes in programming courses and enhance their metacognition. The results offer insightful information on the patterns of student performance that can guide the creation of instructional interventions that are more successful.

articleTitle: Optimum Accuracy of Software Defect Prediction using Machine Learning Technique
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Focus of the paper is on predicting software defects (SD) based on Machine learning (ML) techniques which is a challenging research area because of unbalanced nature of data sets. In general, a set of design metrics is used for fault prediction and for identifying the fault-proneness in software and recent studies shows that ML techniques is being applied for defect prediction. However, some ML techniques cannot produce the needed results when dealing with unbalanced dataset and the results produced are not certainly inferred by the developers by observing these factors, we propose a unique approach for fault prediction which is based on feature selection technique which improves the overall performance by using attribute selection when predicting defects. The ML concentrates on the algorithms entirely centred on statistical methods and data mining techniques for classifying and predicting the defects and these statistical methods followed are quite similar to regression based methods which we used earlier to the ML. When more data is available, ML algorithms behave as dynamic algorithms to improve their performance significantly. The DT ML technique is providing good accuracy compared to other NB and SVM technique. In this model is simulated python language and calculated simulation parameter i.e. precision, recall and accuracy.

articleTitle: Fusion of PSO and Dijkstra Approach for Efficient Routing Among IoT Devices
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Efficient routing is a critical challenge in Internet of Things (IoT) networks due to the vast number of interconnected devices. This paper presents a hybrid approach that combines Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and the Dijkstra algorithm to enhance routing efficiency. PSO optimizes the selection of paths by considering multiple criteria, while Dijkstra’s algorithm ensures the shortest path in a deterministic manner. The fusion of these techniques leads to better route optimization, reducing latency and energy consumption in IoT networks. The proposed hybrid model PSO + Dijkstra (PSOD) algorithm is evaluated in a simulation environment, showing significant improvements in routing performance compared to traditional methods.

articleTitle: Performance Enhancement of Power System Through Fuzzy Controlled GUPFC
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: The system stability and power quality are the most incredibly essential requirement for a power system. Utility electricity supply help in meeting the load demands of consumers in a clean and efficient manner. FACTS devices are developed to feed customers while preserving the stability of the power system during failures. This research work presents stability examination of distribution system with and without GUPFC when various faults occur. The results obtained using MATLAB/SIMULINK for such system configurations are presented in this work. It is found that GUPFC successfully mitigates voltage sag occurring during fault conditions and helps in performance enhancement of the 5 bus distribution system and thus ensures quality of power supply being delivered to all load buses.

articleTitle: Exploratory data analysis to study the impact of MGNREGA on employment generation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) was designed the enhance the livelihood of rural households all across India, providing opportunities for wage employment. In recent years the program has faced a lot of challenges in terms of providing 100 days of employment to all the rural households. There has been a decline in wage employment opportunities beyond the year 2020-2021, due to ineffective management practices. In order to dive deeper into the issue, the researcher performs data-driven analysis of the MGNREGA scheme utilizing the open-source data available in the MGNREGA official website, focusing on the years 2014 to 2024, exploring the contributing factors for the decline in the scheme’s effectiveness. The researcher uncovers hidden valuable insights and visually represented them, by performing Exploratory Data Analysis on the data obtained. The data and insights generated are visually represented by employing various python libraries in Jupyter Notebook, identifying trends, correlations among variables and patterns, as well as shedding light on the scheme’s performance and area of improvement. By performing in depth analysis and visualization of the data, the researcher aims to provide valuable insights on the effectiveness and challenges faced by the MGNREGA scheme, ensuring effective implementation of the scheme. Ensuring the improvement in the economic wellbeing and livelihoods of the rural communities across India, the insights gained from the visual representation of the data, allows the policy makers to take well informed decisions, ultimately ensuring the scheme’s success.

articleTitle: AI Enhanced Anesthesia Dosing: Evaluating ML Models
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is revolutionizing health-care, particularly in the field of anesthesiology. This paper evaluates the application of AI-enhanced models in optimizing anesthesia dosing to improve patient outcomes and operational efficiency. By integrating machine learning (ML) techniques, we analyze structured and unstructured patient data to predict anesthesia needs, automate drug delivery, and monitor vital signs in real time. The study examines several ML models, such as Support Vector Machines, Decision Trees, and Gradient Boosting, assessing their accuracy in predicting anesthetic requirements. The results show that AI can effectively reduce human error, enhance decision-making, and improve patient safety during perioperative care. The paper discusses the system architecture, data collection methods, and model performance, emphasizing the future potential of AI in automating anesthesia processes.

articleTitle: Vulnerability Assessment of XOR Arbiter PUFs: ML Attacks on Lightweight Security Primitives
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Physical Unclonable Functions (PUFs) generate unique, unpredictable challenge-response pairs (CRPs), making them essential for device authentication and secure key generation [1]. Among various architectures, XOR Arbiter PUFs enhance security by combining multiple arbiter outputs through XOR operations. However, their robustness is increasingly undermined by machine learning (ML) attacks. This paper presents a novel, resource-optimized training algorithm specifically designed for constrained environments, significantly reducing computational demands while achieving 100% prediction accuracy on publicly available XOR Arbiter PUF datasets. The proposed approach highlights critical vulnerabilities in XOR PUFs, underscoring the need for improved architectural designs to mitigate security risks in sensitive applications.

articleTitle: Enhanced Cassava Plant Disease Detection and Classification using ANN
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: To implement an Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) based Plant Leaf Disease Detection System using MATLAB. On time detection of plant diseases is a very important element in maintaining the health and continuity of crops to prevent the threaten that could harm agriculture engine. It is a system based on image processing to analyze plant leaves to detect diseases. Plant leaves are then captured as high-resolution images, and the key features (color, texture, shape) of the plant leaves are extracted to separate healthy plants from infected plans. Subsequently ANN model is trained with these extracted features to identify the type and level of disease. The model created is developed to detect different plant diseases through a dataset containing labeled images. MATLAB is used as a powerful computational environment to design the ANN, fine tune its parameters and test the operation accuracy. Farmers and agricultural experts can use the approach to identify plant diseases early on, which means they can benefit from timely intervention, reducing crop loss. This combined system linked to smart connected agricultural tools presents a highly scalable approach in monitoring and management of diseases in modern farming practices.

articleTitle: VTU Question Classification System based on BERT and Bloom’s Taxonomy Ring’
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: The "VTU Question Classification System Based on BERT and Bloom’s Taxonomy" integrates advanced Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques to automate the classification of questions related to education. Utilizing the BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers) model, the system aims to categorize questions into respective cognitive levels as defined by Bloom’s Taxonomy. This initiative addresses the challenges of manual question classification, which is often time-consuming and prone to errors. The application encompasses stages of data gathering, preprocessing, model fine-tuning, and developing an accessible user interface. The expected outcomes include an efficient NLP system capable of accurately classifying questions, thereby aiding in aligning educational assessments with specific learning objectives. This work contributes to the enhancement of educational assessment techniques and offers potential for future advancements in the application of NLP in education.

articleTitle: Vision Transformer-Based Automated Classification of Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: ALL, or Acute Lymphoblastic Leukaemia, is an acute leukaemia disease characterized by white blood cell malignancy, most commonly found in children. Conventional diagnosis requires higher-order laboratory testing procedures that are rather cumbersome and costly. In recent times, deep learning research has marked outstanding performances for automation in medical image analyses that facilitate quick and correct diagnosis. In this work, we proposed a deep learning-based model with the Vision Transformer architecture to classify ALL from peripheral blood smear images. It performed very well on the test set with an accuracy of 99.69% and hence proved to be efficient in identifying ALL with a high degree of precision. Additionally, we employed Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) to enhance the explainability of the model's predictions, providing visual insights into the regions of blood smear images that influenced the classification decisions. This integration of explainable AI (XAI) ensures transparency and builds trust in the model's predictions, making it more clinically acceptable. The performance and interpretability of the ViT-based model indicate that it may revolutionize the diagnostic practices in hematological malignancies by offering a scalable, efficient, and explainable diagnostic solution.

articleTitle: Animal Sound Classification for Wildlife Surveillance
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Wildlife conservation is very important to help monitor animal populations and behaviors, aiding conservation efforts, especially for endangered species.This study presents an non-intrusive animal sound classification system, which utilizes preprocessing techniques to extract Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) from sound files using the LibROSA library. This is then used to classify the animal sounds using various deep learning models. A dataset of 8000 animal sound samples from 10 different animal types was collected from an online sound source site for training and testing the system. The results show that the proposed system achieved a high accuracy of 96.3% in classifying animal sounds using Random forest classifier. Index Terms—animal sound classification, wildlife surveillance, Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC), LibROSA library

articleTitle: Campus Grid: A Technological Solution for Enhanced Coordination in Campus-Wide Activities
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Campus Grid presents an innovative technical solution which is designed to enhance coordination across various campus wide activities. The educational institutions lack an integrated platform to coordinate various activities within the campus like managing academic schedules, events and collaboration. So there is a growing need for a unified platform which is used to foster seamless interaction among students, faculties and administrators. This project introduces a multi-functional website and mobile app to coordinate various activities. The key features of this project are event creation and sharing, attendance tracking, exam hall plan generator, classroom management and real time notifications for changes in academic activities. Furthermore, through this application the students can collaborate with each other and form study groups and discussion forums to clarify their doubts. The teachers can upload notes, create study plans, learning milestones and they can also track the progress of students. It also offers advanced features such as internship and job offer listings to make students aware of various opportunities available. The main motive of this platform is to coordinate various activities into one single platform such that it will be very useful for the users to manage. The potential impact of Campus Grid not only within individual institutions but also promotes inter college collaboration and resource sharing thereby this application develops a more supportive community.

articleTitle: WanderVision : Enhancing Dementia Care with Artificial Intelligence and Augmented Reality
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: This paper is an advanced application of Augmented Reality to form an intelligent navigation system designed for support towards individuals with dementia. This system aims to identify and mark paths that are safe in guiding users through complex environments and, ultimately, toward a safer and more immersive experience in navigation. Assisted with occlusion handling it will be able to enhance user awareness by overlaying critical safety cues within the user's field of view dynamically. This is even more enhanced beyond just the aspect of navigation, as with the integration of computer vision technologies, providing solutions on medicinal and dietary requirements supporting lifestyle choices towards a healthier living and personal safety. Concentration on safety and assistance towards health issues adequately comes under the general scope of the project, which may help ensure greater independence and personal autonomy in the lives of persons with dementia-managing life's routine activities or dealing with episodes of cognitive disorientation. This AR-based system would directly deliver personalized health and safety insights to users with an aim to enhance the autonomy and resilience of individuals with dementia, providing practical support in leading safer, more empowered lives.

articleTitle: Metrics-Based Refactoring Prediction Using Boosting Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Software quality enhancement can be done by identifying the refactoring scope of the existing open-source projects in real time. The refactoring mechanism alters the internal structure of the code base without changing the external result. Objectives: In this work, we have assured the project quality by considering different source code metrics as input that helps to evaluate the refactoring score. Methodology: Software metrics used are NOI, SLOC, LOC, WMC, and CCL are considered as input parameters and implemented five different types of boosting algorithms. Result Analysis: As there are many extra features, we have selected 20 relevant features out of 115 using Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE). It is observed that Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGB) is best suitable for identifying refactoring opportunities with an accuracy of 99%.Conclusion: A comparison of projects is performed and Titan projects highly required refactoring as it contains more dirty code.

articleTitle: Block Krylov Subspace Methods for Scalable Deep Graph Convolutional Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: In this paper, I explore the application of block Krylov subspace methods to enhance the scalability and efficiency of deep graph convolutional networks (GCNs). Deep learning models, particularly GCNs, have gained significant attention for their capability to process graph-structured data; however, they often face challenges related to scalability, over smoothing, and the preservation of informative features in deeper architectures. To address these challenges, I leverage the block Krylov matrix framework, demonstrating that any graph convolution operation characterized by well-defined analytic spectral filters can be reformulated as the product of a block Krylov matrix with learnable parameters. This innovative approach allows for the effective representation of multi-scale information, thereby preserving both local and global features of graph nodes while simultaneously mitigating the over-smoothing phenomenon that frequently arises in deep GCNs.

articleTitle: Improved Emotion Analysis in Tweets through an Ensemble Model [SVM-BERTweet]
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: The paper demonstrates the pivotal function of automatic emotion recognition in knowledge human feelings at scale. Through a comprehensive evaluation of tweets, this research uncovers treasured insights into customer sentiments, permitting packages in advertising strategies, customer support enhancement, and stock market predictions. Furthermore, the have a look at highlights the essential implications of emotion detection in mental fitness by means of figuring out individuals exhibiting symptoms of despair or distress through their tweets. Additionally, the studies explores the potential of this generation in detecting social troubles including bullying outbreaks and terrorist threats, contributing significantly to the field of virtual safety.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Impact of Soil Properties and Climate Conditions on Crop Yield Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: In this paper, we aim to predict the suitable crop using machine learning repressors. Predicting the right crop is one of the challenging tasks because the different soil conditions can improve agricultural output. Predicting the right crop may help to increase agricultural productivity, optimize resource utilization, and promote sustainability. In this study, we considered the different features like Nitrogen (N), Phosphorus (P), Potassium (K), pH, electrical conductivity (EC), organic carbon (OC), and various micronutrients. Our model recommends a suitable crop for the given set of features. Material/Method: The machine learning Regressor classifiers (Linear Regressor, Random Forest Regressor, Support vector Regressor, XGBoost Regressor, Gradient Boosting Regressor, LightGBM, CatBoost, and stacked Regressor) are used. During implementation, we have estimated the performance of metrics like: - Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Mean Squared Error (MSE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), and R-squared (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) to assess the accuracy of the model. Result: The experimental observation reveals that the Stacked Regressor performed very well compared to other classifiers. It has the lowest MAE (3.282), MSE (14.633), and RMSE (3.825) as well as the highest R-squared value of 0.170567. Other classifiers are also exhibited well but they are not up to the mark to select as the best classifiers. A stacked regressor is one of the ensemble learning approaches that enhance the model ability and choose the suitable crop based on soil properties.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Steering Angle Prediction for Autonomous Driving
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: This study explores the use of deep learning for steering angle prediction in autonomous vehicles using camera images as input. The proposed system leverages a convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture inspired by NVIDIA’s model for end-to-end self-driving. A balanced dataset of driving ages and corresponding steering angles is used, with extensive preprocessing and augmentation techniques, including zooming, panning, brightness adjustments, and flipping, to enhance data diversity and generalization. The model is trained using a batch generator to efficiently preprocess and augment images in real time. The architecture includes convolutional layers for feature extraction and fully connected layers for predicting steering angles. Experiments show effective learning, with minimized training and validation losses and accurate prediction of steering angles. This work provides a foundation for improving steering angle prediction by integrating advanced augmentation techniques and modern deep-learning models, aiming to bridge the gap between simulation and real-world driving conditions. Future work includes expanding to multi-camera setups and incorporating temporal data for improved decision-making in dynamic environments.

articleTitle: Machine Learning for Fraud Detection in Banking Cyber security Performance Evaluation of Classifiers and Their Real-Time Scalability
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Context: With the rise of fraudulent activity in banking systems, effective fraud detection measures have become critical to safeguarding financial security and customer trust. Machine learning techniques are commonly used to improve detection capabilities, however their efficacy varies by performance parameter. Understanding these variances is crucial for optimizing fraud detection systems for real-world use. Objectives: Our main aim of this paper is to detect fraud in banking cybersecurity using machine learning classifiers. Materials/Methods: In this paper, we have used several machine learning classifiers to detect fraudulent behavior in the banking system. We used classifiers like: - Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, K-Nearest Neighbors, Gradient Boosting, AdaBoost, and Decision Tree. We have estimated these classifiers' performance metrics like: - accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-scoire. Result: From the experimental observation we found that RF gives the highest accuracy of 0.985, Recall at 0.985000 and the classifier KNN has the highest score at 0.988937. It indicates that RF is the best classifier in comparison to others for detecting fraud in the banking system Simultaneously the classifiers AdaBoost and Gradient Boosting provide good precision and AUC-ROC values

articleTitle: Maternal risk prediction by early detection of Pre-Eclampsia and high-risk pregnancies using machine learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: After 20 weeks of pregnancy, pre-eclampsia, a severe pregnancy syndrome, usually manifests as increased blood pressure and injury to other organs. In order to prevent adverse consequences for both the mother and the fetus, early detection and forecasting are essential for prompt intervention and therapy. Machine learning techniques are highly effective tools for predictive analytics in the healthcare industry, with the ability to identify high-risk pregnancies and enhance clinical decision-making. In this study, it has been suggested that machine learning be used to forecast pre-eclampsia by utilizing clinical and perinatal demographic information. We use a dataset containing information on maternal age, blood pressure readings, and other relevant parameters to train and evaluate predictive models. Artificial neural networks were found to be the most effective approach, achieving an accuracy of 75%, demonstrating their potential in accurately predicting pre-eclampsia and supporting timely medical interventions.

articleTitle: Enhancing Vertical Transport Safety Through an IoT-Based System
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Vertical transportation systems, such as elevators and escalators, are essential components of modern infrastructure, necessitating robust safety mechanisms to ensure user well-being. This paper proposes an Internet of Things (IoT)-based system to enhance the safety, monitoring, and efficiency of vertical transport. The system addresses critical issues, such as sudden elevator cable failures leading to entrapment or uncontrolled descent, power losses during operation, and fire hazards caused by material friction. By leveraging IoT technology, the system enables real-time monitoring and immediate notification of potential problems via messaging. The implementation requires components such as ultrasonic sensors, smoke sensors, vibration sensors, microcontrollers, DC motors, batteries, relays, and the UBIDOT application. The resulting system is low-cost, user-friendly, and economically viable, making it accessible to individuals with minimal technical expertise. Furthermore, it is designed for ease of construction and troubleshooting, offering a practical and scalable solution to improve elevator safety and reliability.

articleTitle: Chernobyl-Inspired Optimization for Efficient Wireless Sensor Network Routing
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Optimising routing in Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) is crucial for enhancing their performance, with a focus on energy conservation, reliable data transmission, and network stability. This research presents a unique approach to WSN routing optimization using Chernobyl Disaster Optimization (CDO), a nature-inspired algorithm modeled on the rehabilitation and ecological restoration efforts following the Chernobyl incident. CDO simulates the process of resource redistribution and recovery after a catastrophic event to identify optimal routing paths in WSNs. The study assesses the CDO algorithm's effectiveness against the traditional Gravitational Search Algorithm (GSA) using key performance indicators such as energy usage, jitter, average end-to-end delay (EED), packet loss, and packet delivery fraction (PFD). Simulation results show that the CDO-based routing optimisation method consistently surpasses GSA, delivering improved end-to-end delay, decreased jitter, reduced packet loss, and enhanced energy efficiency. This investigation highlights CDO's potential as a viable alternative to conventional optimisation techniques, offering a more efficient and adaptable solution for WSN routing optimisation, particularly in dynamic, large-scale scenarios.

articleTitle: Construction and Optimization of Regular Expressions in Genetic Sequence Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: In this paper a novel approach for generating and optimizing regular expressions for genetic sequences is presented. The proposed technique introduces a systematic process to create initial regular expressions, compress and optimize them, and validate their accuracy for sequence matching. The method ensures a precise and reliable match with the given sequences while reducing complexity through an efficient optimization process. The proposed approach is versatile, being applicable to DNA, RNA, protein sequences, or any formal language processing. The method has been tested using a set of sequences with lengths ranging from 64 to 512 characters, with 50-100 pseudo-random generated sequence pairs and 5-10 % mutations for each case. Although the regular expression optimization process consumes slightly more time compared to conventional methods, it significantly reduces the overall matching time. Additionally, the optimized regular expressions show a reduction in memory usage. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach is highly effective for Motif Discovery and Representation, Pattern Matching Algorithms, Comparative Genomics and Phylogenetic and Gene Regulation, and Promoter Analysis, making it suitable for applications in bioinformatics and computational linguistics.

articleTitle: Enhancing Ransomware Detection - A Comparative Review of XGBoost, Random Forest, and Neural Network Approaches
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Ransomware detection has now become an essential challenge in cybersecurity as attackers use using smart and tricky methods to get interrupts our simple defences. This review discusses how the work of leading machine learning (ML) models like, XGBoost, Random Forest (RF), and Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs), improves ransomware detection systems. The most prominent reason why XGBoost has been selected as the model is because of its high accuracy rate, and random forests are considered due to their appreciation for model stability, which is why they have been used within studies for efficient base classifiers for most of them. ANNs also offer a strong nonlinear approach when handling ransomware's complex data patterns. In this paper, we evaluate some of these approaches- hybrids that include XGBoost and RF algorithms as well as advanced ANNs configurations for their very distinct strengths and weaknesses in the sense of ransomware detection. In synthesizing the results, The review explains how applicable and comparatively advantageous these approaches are at detecting ransomware. The study ultimately seeks to guide future implementations by summarizing key model features, evaluation metrics, and adaptability to evolving ransomware behaviours, there by contributing to enhanced cybersecurity frameworks.

articleTitle: Footstep Powered Energy Harvesting System
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: This paper explores the applicability of human kinetic energy in charging portable devices. Piezoelectric sensors are installed in a walkway or a mat where mechanical energy of footsteps is converted into electrical energy. This energy once harvested goes through a number of electronic elements such as power conditioning circuits together with amplifiers in order to generate the right voltage and worth of current required in charging portable gadgets. The system consists of an inverting amplifier, a buck converter, an LCD display, a microcontroller, an ADC, a piezoelectric sensor and a battery. The piezoelectric sensor applies a voltage when pressure is exerted such as that which occurs when someone is walking. The ADC samples the voltage and converts it into a digital signal; the microcontroller then processes it. The microcontroller monitors battery charge, charges batteries when necessary and displays related information on the LCD. This way the voltage of the battery is regulated by the buck converter to an ideal voltage suitable for charging mobile devices. The suggested strategy is an innovative and efficient means of charging mobile devices in the public domains and other busy centers. This makes this technology to enhance the future to be more sustainable and green by using power from renewable resources and by reducing the extent to which it depended on conventional outlets.While the core concept of piezoelectric energy harvesting from human footsteps is promising, several challenges and considerations need to be addressed for widespread implementation: Efficiency and Power Output: Improving the geometrical configuration and the material properties to achieve the highest efficiency from the sensors. Searching for potential new circuit configurations able to reduce power losses at the period of energy conversion and storage. Based on such aspects like flow of feet traffic, the load balance, and environment conditions to improve the system efficiency.Durability and Reliability: Designing safe structures that will not wear out easily that can easily be applied in areas that are torn and crowded. Adopting that suitable parts should be used for the design and use of strong packages to facilitate long-term functions. Cultivating approaches on how to prevent much downtime or avoid shortening the lifespan of systems much.Cost-Effectiveness: Economies of scale and product with regards to manufacturing cost could be addressed. Identifying potential for application of less expensive materials and elements without luxating performance. Knowing where to get funds for the training program and other incentives provided by the government to scholars and researchers. Parking lots and garages will be handy to charge electric cars, for instance, by means of an external wall or through wired connections. To supply power to the sensors and the communication equipment in various smart cities. Residential and Commercial Buildings: For charging small power devices such as lighting, security systems and other low power gadgets in our homes or offices.Producing power supply in central zones. Wearable Technology: Energy for smartwatches, fitness trackers, and other wearable electronic appliances. Delaying time between recharging and also improving battery longevity. Remote and Off-Grid Applications: Supplement power for recommended electric appliances in areas where power supply is very rare. Promoting and implementing sustainable development while enhancing the living standards of the people that are off the grid.

articleTitle: AI Enabled Virtualization and Fault Detection in Machines
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Modern machines like automobile, PC, mobile, and wearable machines are prone to inefficient and unreliable fault detection and service. Service providers are mostly at the wrong end due to vague diagnostics and repair processes. It aims to design an AI-based fault detection and servicing system that will boost the accuracy, transparency, and efficiency of several devices when faults are detected and rectified. It involves fault detection through machine learning models, analysis of sensor data and performance logs, and comparison with ideal benchmarks. Virtualization is achieved by creating 3D models from image processing to visualize and explain faults. Virtual calibration is also implemented through a virtual simulation environment for device testing and calibration before manual repair. This physical mapping is integrated by real-time sensor data for continuous monitoring and mapping of device states. The outcome shows that the AI-based system increased the accuracy of fault detection, provided clear visual explanations, and made it easy and quick to repair while minimizing the downtime of users as well as creating trust in service providers. It enhances the fault detection and servicing process of modern machines, with much more effective diagnostics, transparent explanations, and efficient repairs for the satisfaction of the customers.

articleTitle: Emerging Trends in Software Engineering: Implications for Development and Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: This study explores recent advancements in software engineering, focusing on methods and practices that enhance development efficiency, security, and innovation. The originality of this research lies in its comprehensive analysis of the latest trends, such as Agile methodologies, and the integration of machine learning, which are revolutionizing the software development landscape. The primary objective is to assess the effectiveness of these trends in optimizing software development processes and improving end-user experiences. This research applies quantitative analysis, using time-series data and survey responses from software development teams to evaluate key performance indicators associated with each trend. The analysis, conducted using SPSS software, examines correlations between the adoption of modern methodologies and outcomes such as reduced development time, enhanced security, and overall software quality. Findings indicate that Agile and DevOps practices contribute significantly to faster deployment cycles, while machine learning integration aids in predictive analysis, improving error detection and reducing maintenance needs. The practical implications of this study emphasize the value of embracing emerging methodologies to foster innovation, enhance project success rates, and ensure robust software products. These insights aim to support software companies and developers in adopting strategic trends for sustainable and effective engineering solutions.

articleTitle: Adaptive KOA: Leaf disease classification using hyperspectral images for Internet of Things (IoT)-based sustainable agriculture
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: In recent times, the crops as well as the agriculture management is one of the important field to watch out, therefore the image processing business provide more benefit to the crops along with support precaution needs. In this research, an adaptive Kookaburra Optimization Algorithm (Adaptive KOA) is implemented for leaf disease classification using hyperspectral images for Sustainable Agriculture in IoT.At first, the IoT modelis replicated and the routing is conductedto transmit the data from source to the Base Station (BS). Moreover, in BS the following steps are conducted. The input hyperspectral image (HSI)is subjected to a band selection module. The band selection is done using the implemented Adaptive Kookaburra Optimization Algorithm (Adaptive KOA). The developed Adaptive KOA is devised by incorporating Adaptive concept with Kookaburra Optimization Algorithm (KOA). The Selected bands are fed into the leaf segmentation module, where the Deep Embedded Clustering (DEC) technique is utilized for segmentation. Fusion of segmented image from different bands is carried out by the majority voting method. Finally, Leaf disease classification is carried out based on the 3D-Convolutional Neural Network (3DCNN) into normal and abnormal cases. The developed Adaptive KOA-3DCNN method has the maximum value for accuracy as 0.917%, highest value for True negative rate(TNR)as 0.927%, highest value for True positive rate (TPR) as 0.907%.

articleTitle: Gastrointestinal Lung Cancer Disease Classification via Hybrid Deep Architecture Trained with Improved Pattern Features
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: In the initial stage of lung cancer, GI tract is not frequently the position of metastases. It may be challenging to distinguish pulmonary metastases from the gastrointestinal (GI) tract and primary lung cancer. The following stages are followed to classify the gastrointestinal lung cancer disease: Image acquisition, preprocessing, feature extraction, and classification. The process of collecting images is called image acquisition. As per the work, the benchmark dataset is under consideration. Gaussian filtering is used to preprocess the input image for further processing. Subsequently, the features that are retrieved in the Feature Extraction step include Shape feature, Multi texton features, Improved median Binary Pattern, and Local Gradient Increasing Pattern (LGIP). A hybrid model trained with the extracted features will be used for classification, which integrates Squeezenet and LSTM models. The results of the proposed work is compared over the conventional models in terms of different performance measures.

articleTitle: Enhanced Electrocardiogram Data Compression and Classification Using 2D Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: The task of electrocardiogram (ECG) classification is a combination of data compression and classification of signals based on the patient’s health. This paper introduces a novel technique for compressing electrocardiogram (ECG) images and utilizing these compressed images for accurate classification. We transform ECG signals into images and compress them to reduce their size while preserving classification accuracy significantly. Our approach employs a 2-dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (2-D CNN) model and achieves an impressive accuracy of 97% even after compressing the images by up to 76%. The proposed technique was tested on the widely-used MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Dataset, demonstrating its robustness and efficacy. Maintaining high classification accuracy despite significant image compression is crucial for efficient storage and transmission in resource-constrained environments. This method holds substantial potential for real-time monitoring and diagnosis in telemedicine applications, emphasizing the importance of our contribution to the field.

articleTitle: Real-Time Energy Consumption Insights for Hospitals with IoT and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Reducing operating expenses and minimizing environmental effects requires efficient hospital energy management. This research provides a comprehensive approach for tracking and analyzing energy consumption in real time. With the Internet of Things (IoT) and Machine Learning, especially Support Vector Regression (SVR). Energy consumption, environmental factors, and operating parameters are continually monitored by the proposed system's network of IoT sensors. A centralized cloud platform receives data streams from these sensors in real-time, with high resolution. A powerful machine learning method, SVR, processes and analyzes data. It is well known for its accuracy in predicting continuous variables. SVR models energy consumption trends, spot outliers, and predict future energy use. The predictive features of the system allow hospital managers to spot inefficiencies, forecast peak energy needs, and take proactive actions to optimize energy consumption. Energy data can be easily interpreted, and decisions can be made with the help of the system's visualization and analytics features. This system's combination of IoT and SVR offers a scalable and inexpensive method to improve healthcare facilities' energy efficiency. According to experimental data from pilot installations, there was a notable improvement in overall energy management techniques and a considerable decrease in energy waste. According to this research, modern IoT and machine learning technology may drive sustainable hospital operations and environmental stewardship.

articleTitle: Application of Optimized Artificial Neural Networks to Enhance Medical Data Interpolation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: This study implements a K- Nearest Neighbors Model using the Heart Disease Prediction Dataset, and then intentionally introduces missing values by replacing around 300 original cholesterol (chol) values with NaN (Not a Number) values. Further, an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) model has been deployed upon the dataset to predict these missing chol values based on other features using linear interpolation techniques. This prediction is subsequently compared against the original chol values that were initially present in the dataset. Various visualizations and comparisons have been carried out through scatter plots, which allow for analyzing the proximity of the predicted chol values to the original ones, considering the interplay between other dataset features and the remaining chol values. This study contributes to the field of medical sciences and machine learning, showing the importance of accurate interpolation of data values in case of missing or inadequate data points in medical datasets.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Various Deep Learning Models for Sign Language Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: This study investigates the application of deep learning for automatic recognition of American Sign Language (ASL) alphabets and numbers (0-10). Utilizing a Kaggle dataset comprising 2,520 images representing 36 unique ASL signs, we processed the images by resizing them to 64 x 64 pixels and dividing them into training and testing subsets to maintain balanced learning. We assessed the performance of various convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures, including a basic CNN, VGG-16, and ResNet-50, for feature extraction and classification. The models were evaluated using essential performance metrics accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score to ensure their robustness and reliability. Among these models, ResNet-50 achieved the highest performance with an accuracy of 94.05%. This research highlights the potential of deep learning to facilitate communication between the Deaf and hard-of-hearing communities and the general public through rapid, automated ASL recognition, contributing to a more inclusive communication solution.

articleTitle: Indian Gross Domestic Product Per Capita Prediction based on Economic Indicators
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: This paper is about identifying the contributing socio-economic indicators that affect the Gross Domestic Product Per Capita of India with historical data from 1960 to 2021 and build a methodology to predict the Gross Domestic Product per capita based on the contributing factors. To predict India's GDP per capita, an ensemble prediction was used, which included Support Vector Regression (SVR), the Extreme Gradient Boosting Model, and the ARIMA Model. It is critical to forecast GDP per capita and its influencing factors for better policy formulation, resource allocation, risk management, investment decisions, long-term planning, social welfare, and other purposes. This paper could contribute to encouraging long-term economic growth and improve citizens' quality of life. The findings of this paper provide an in-depth understanding of the intricate relationship between socioeconomic indicators and Gross Domestic Product in India.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: An Empirical Literature Review on Multi Class Data Stream Learning with Class Imbalance Problem in Real World Data Sources
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Data mining and knowledge discovery is one of the cutting-edge fields in science and technology for identifying pressing issues in real world. The amount of data collected has increased due to the quick development of technology and the low cost of internet access. One of the difficult problems is analyzing the massive volume of data that comes in from various data streams. Machine learning research has primarily concentrated on binary classification data problems with high unbalanced data from the earliest literatures published on till recently. When it comes to processing data streams effectively, research on highly unbalanced multi-class data is still mostly underdeveloped. This study focuses on reviews of the models or methods for dealing with extremely unbalanced multi-class data, as well as their advantages and disadvantages and related fields. The objectives of this article are to: comprehend the trend of highly imbalanced multi-class data through examination of related literatures; to analyze the traditional and contemporary approaches to handling highly imbalanced multi-class data; and develop a framework for highly imbalanced multi-class data. After doing the chosen highly imbalanced multi-class dataset analysis and adapting it to the most recent machine learning algorithms or approaches, there will be talks on unresolved issues and the way highly imbalanced multi-class data should go in the future.

articleTitle: Establishing a Balance between Precision and Openness in AI Systems for Essential Decision-Making: Interpretable Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: A growing number of industries, like healthcare, banking, and autonomous systems, are placing their trust in AI systems to make important decisions, which calls for the creation of models that are transparent and have high predictive precision. In this research, we concentrate on interpretable deep learning models as a means to tackle the overarching problem of making AI systems both precise and open (interpretable). Despite the remarkable accuracy that deep learning models have shown in areas like medical diagnostics, image recognition, and natural language processing, the lack of transparency, accountability, and trust caused by their "black-box" nature is a major concern, particularly when decisions with potentially life-changing implications are at stake. There are ethical questions about justice, prejudice, and explainability brought up by the absence of interpretability, which also makes it harder for regulated areas to use AI. The goal of this study is to investigate possible approaches that can make deep learning models both very accurate and easily interpretable. To help non-technical stakeholders better comprehend model predictions, we explore state-of-the-art strategies including attention mechanisms, layer-wise relevance propagation, and post-hoc explanation methods (e.g., SHAP, LIME). Combining model-based and data-driven decision-making, we also provide new architectures that intrinsically promote openness. In addition, the study delves into the costs and benefits of model performance against interpretability, looking at how interpretability limitations might affect accuracy and how accuracy could affect interpretability. Several real-world case studies are used to assess these trade-offs. These case studies include autonomous driving systems, financial fraud detection, and predictive healthcare analytics. All of these systems need to be highly accurate and interpretable in order to meet regulatory requirements and maintain user trust. Based on our research, interpretable models have the potential to perform similarly to opaque models while also offering further advantages including increased user trust, simpler debugging, and compliance with legal and ethical requirements. Contributing to the continuing conversation on responsible AI, this study provides developers and legislators with practical insights by outlining a methodology for striking a balance between transparency and accuracy. The goal of future research is to enhance these methods even further by combining symbolic reasoning with neural network topologies to create hybrid models that are both accurate and easy to understand. This effort could improve the transparency and accountability of AI systems, which could speed up their use in high-stakes decision-making situations.

articleTitle: Neuromorphic Computing Architectures for Enhanced Signal Processing in Autonomous Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Innovative computing techniques that strike a balance between speed, efficiency, and adaptability are required due to the growing complexity of signal processing in autonomous systems. Neuromorphic computing, which draws inspiration from the structure of the human brain, offers a workable method for enhancing signal processing in real-time analysis and decision-making devices, including robotic systems, drones, and driverless cars. The integration of neuromorphic architectures for sophisticated signal processing in robotic systems, drones, and autonomous cars is examined in this research. The application of event-driven processing and spiking neural networks (SNNs) for real-time analysis and decision-making is the main emphasis of the research. The approach involves developing a scalable neuromorphic framework that makes use of cutting-edge hardware, including neuromorphic chips, and evaluating its reaction time, energy efficiency, and processing speed in comparison to traditional von Neumann architectures. Neuromorphic systems demonstrate their potential for continuous real-time data handling by reducing latency by 30% and improving energy efficiency by up to 50%. The system's resilience in handling intricate environmental signals and adjusting to changing inputs is highlighted by important findings. According to the paper's conclusion, incorporating neuromorphic designs greatly improves autonomous systems' efficiency and real-time processing capabilities, opening the door to more responsive and energy-efficient operations. Improving hardware compatibility and broadening applications across various autonomous technologies are two areas of future research.

articleTitle: IoT-Driven Environmental Pollution Monitoring with a Deep Attentional Hybrid Transformer Model
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: As urbanization and globalization increase, air quality in many parts of the world is deteriorating and need quick action. Many cities have unacceptable levels of particulate matter and gaseous pollution, exceeding government and WHO guidelines. Continuous air pollution exposure increases the prevalence and mortality of respiratory disorders like asthma and COPD. Data preparation, feature extraction, and model training are the study's three steps. A neighbor-based feature scaling method prepares data for processing. Feature selection removes superfluous data before model training. The sophisticated architecture of the CTransNet model speeds up training. This strategy outperforms others, notably for attention-based models and CNNs. The model's 93.56% accuracy beats stateof-the-art alternatives. These findings demonstrate that the proposed technique can accurately predict air quality, which could enhance health by warning of imminent pollution.

articleTitle: Chronic Kidney Disease Prediction using U-Net Architecture
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: A worldwide health concern, chronic kidney disease (CKD) must be detected early to optimize patient outcomes. The ability of conventional diagnostic techniques to identify early-stage CKD is limited. For precise kidney segmentation and CKD prediction from MRI/CT images, a U-Net architecture is proposed in the paper. Large Important performance indicators are used to assess the performance of the model once it has been trained using a dataset. In comparison to earlier techniques like CNN-based models with 88.4% accuracy and hybrid CNN-RNN architectures with 93.7% accuracy, the U-Net model obtained 95.6% accuracy, 94.8% precision, 93.4% recall, and a 94.1% F1-score. Using MATLAB Simulink, the model was implemented in real-time for kidney segmentation and CKD risk prediction. The findings demonstrate that the U-Net model outperforms other models in CKD identification, providing a dependable tool for clinical application. To increase accuracy, future work will concentrate on improving the model's early-stage CKD detection capabilities and investigating 3D U-Net designs.

articleTitle: Mamba-Hybrid Language Models: Advancing Detection of AI-Generated Text in Academic Contexts
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: The emergence of ChatGPT, an advanced generative artificial intelligence (AI) tool, has posed significant challenges to academic integrity in educational environments. This paper explores effective approaches and essential strategies to address these challenges, ensuring that educators can uphold standards of honesty and authenticity in student work. This study introduces an efficient language model using Mamba-Hybrid Language Models (MHLMs) algorithms to detecting AI-generated text. In the preprocessing stage, text was standardized through various steps such as lowercase conversion, tokenization, stop-word removal, feature extraction, digit removal, and space elimination to ensure high data quality. Our investigation into distinguishing Essays generated by Large Language Models (LLMs) from those written by students yielded significant findings. Mamba achieves state-of-the-art results on a diverse set of domains, where it matches or exceeds the performance of strong Transformer models. Our results show that while pure Selective state-space models (SSMs) based models match or exceed Transformers on many NLP tasks, MHLMs models lag behind Transformer models on tasks which require strong detection of AI generated and human generated Essays. In contrast, we found that the 10B-parameter MHLMs model outperformed the 8B-parameter Transformer across all standard tasks we evaluated, with an average improvement of +1.25 points. Additionally, MHLMs are projected to be up to 5 times faster in token generation during inference.

articleTitle: Enhancing Livestock Supply Chains with Blockchain Traceability from Source to Market: A Survey
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: This document provides an in-depth analysis of how blockchain technology can greatly improve transparency, traceability, and accountability in fish and livestock supply chains, presenting the potential to transform this industry.
