Utilizing blockchain’s decentralized framework, which guarantees a secure and unchangeable record of transactions, problems associated with inefficiencies, fraud, and data manipulation in conventional supply chains can be efficiently resolved. This survey analyzes the present condition of blockchain applications in fish and livestock management, emphasizing their advantages and drawbacks. Furthermore, it highlights significant technical and regulatory challenges that impede wider acceptance, while recognizing potential future research avenues that could enhance processes from the production stage to the retail stage. The results intend to assist stakeholders in developing supply chains that are more sustainable, efficient, and transparent, fostering trust and complying with regulatory requirements.

articleTitle: Model Checking for Security Assurance in Cyber-Physical Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: The attacks BW-DDoS represent known onslaughts of packets forwarded by large numbers of participating websites that interfere with a valid stream of traffic through congested networks. While such attacks often rely on blunt force that is not even nearly so effective today they are nonetheless capable of a scale much greater than ever in terms of their attack potential, and far worse. When creating defenses against such malicious acts, it is crucial to use several defensive techniques at the same time in order to successfully counter these threats. The necessity for sophisticated defenses is highlighted by the growing threat posed by adversarial assaults and DDoS situations. BW-DDoS takes advantage of flaws in the Internet’s congestion control systems, like TCP and related protocols, which lower network utilization in reaction to packet loss and delays. Such attacks result in serious performance degradation; the server, network, or region can even fall down as a result of such an attack. Such attacks, in the past, were deployed to create gigantic failures in times of a calamity. This paper addresses BW-DDoS attack and protection strategies. Even if the brute-force methods used now are basic, they could become much more successful and harmful in the future. In order to counter these changing threats, the article examines both current defenses and possible new tactics. This summary offers useful information for anyone curious about BW-DDoS attacks and defense strategies.

articleTitle: From Single to Multi-Disease: AI Techniques in Medical Diagnostics
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: The healthcare sector has witnessed a transformative rise in disease diagnosis due to the emergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and other related processes. AI is central to success in healthcare because of the outstanding techniques which are offered by Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL). The optimal diagnosis of disease through these techniques requires medical imaging data like ultrasound, Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), mammography, and many more. This research paper covers a detailed, AI-assisted, medical survey based on the techniques used in identifying various diseases including eye diseases, lung disorders, skin diseases, and neurological disorders inclusive of Alzheimer's and cancer. The study further presents the key highlights, strengths, and limitations of allied techniques along with their result analysis. Along with the single disease prediction, this research paper additionally analyses the techniques on Multi-Disease (MltD) prediction using PRISMA guidelines. Three specific scientific databases including Web of Science (WOS), Scopus, and PubMed are utilized to identify the related articles, and in total 321 articles were obtained. After a thorough screening process, 27 articles are selected for detailed analysis to provide valuable insights for future advancements in MltD prediction models in the healthcare system.

articleTitle: Two-Dimensional Multi-Deep CNNs for Accurate and Robust Software Defect Detection: A Performance-Driven Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Software systems are growing in size and complexity. These properties make software defect prevention challenging. Thus, automatically predicting software module defects can help engineers conserve resources. Several ways have been presented to discover and fix these issues cheaply. However, these solutions may need a performance bump. This paper introduces the Multi-Deep Convolutional Neural Network to improve binary and multi-class software classification. Instead of one-dimensional CNNs, the proposed model captures n-gram characteristics inside and between datasets using a two-dimensional multi-scale convolutional technique. Advanced crow search optimisation algorithm (ACSOA) is used to optimally select model parameters. Besides Apache Active MQ, the study employed Eclipse data sets to evaluate the recommended deep learning method. F1-score, recall, accuracy, and precision were utilized to validate the model. The results show that the suggested strategy finds software vulnerabilities better and more reliably than current models.

articleTitle: IoT Based Battery Monitoring System in Electric Vehicle with Multiple Fault Detection Using AI
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Electric vehicle (EV) batteries face several challenges that can affect performance and safety. Key problems include overheating, which can lead to thermal runaway, and overcharging or deep discharging, which shortens battery life. EV batteries are also vulnerable to issues like capacity degradation over time, reduced performance in extreme temperatures, and potential short circuits or internal faults. The proposed IoT-based electric vehicle (EV) battery monitoring and fault detection system provides real-time analysis and alerts to ensure efficient battery management and safety. To keep an eye on important variables like temperature, voltage, current, and charge levels, this system makes use of Internet of Things sensors built within the battery. Data from these sensors is continuously gathered and sent to a centralized cloud platform for processing in real time. It provides real-time battery parameter monitoring with an accuracy of 95–98%. The system improves fault detection accuracy to 95-98% by employing advanced techniques and continuous monitoring. With the use of predictive analytics and machine learning, it achieves 90-95% accuracy in battery health prediction, ensuring optimal battery performance. The system optimizes power management strategies and control mechanisms, boosting energy efficiency to around 95%. Intelligent charging algorithms ensure 95% effectiveness in preventing battery overcharge. Overall, this system enhances EV battery safety, lifespan, and efficiency.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Solutions with CNN and IoT for Enhancing Visual Impairments
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Visual impairment is a problem that affects millions of people worldwide, preventing them from walking independently and performing daily tasks. Some of the challenges that blind people face include crossing the street, reading, driving, and socializing. Despite the scientific community’s continuous efforts to treat the eye, these solutions have not yet been found. Traditional aids such as canes are useful but limited. Get in the groove. The main focus of the project is to integrate the YOLOv5 object detection model with a convolutional neural network (CNN). Known for its fast and accurate target detection, YOLOv5, together with CNN, improves the physical ability to detect and classify targets in difficult areas with high accuracy. The eye uses the camera module to continuously monitor the environment and identify various objects in real time; the detected data is converted into speech by text-to-speech (TTS) converters such as Google Text- to-Speech (gTTS) and pyttsx3 This description allows users to get an instant description of their surroundings, unlike helping the blind, it improves their ability to navigate independently rather than just providing references, but there are also good ways to work with better and more reliable assistive technologies.

articleTitle: Impact of AI-Driven Personalized Experience in Shaping Consumer Loyalty Towards Quick Commerce
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: This research focuses on exploring the opportunities that AI provide through Responsiveness and website design to improve customer satisfaction and increase the customer loyalty to the quick commerce industry. It also seeks to find out the extent to which the customer satisfaction moderates the relationship between personalization and customer loyalty in AI- enabled quick commerce platforms. Specifically, this study adopts Expectation-Confirmation Theory (ECT) to investigate the ways through which perceived personalisation initiatives spearheaded by AI lead to the fulfilment of consumer expectations, hence satisfaction and brand loyalty. In the present research, Structural Equation Modelling – Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) analysis was conducted based on the data collected from 285 respondents of Mumbai, Bangalore, and New Delhi through snowball sampling. The study adds to the body of knowledge by addressing a research gap that concerns the integration of AI in the context of quick commerce and provides valuable recommendations for the design of the platform and strategies of engaging consumers.

articleTitle: Code Smell Predictions Using Ensemble Deep Learning Approach: A Case Study on Data Class
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Context: The greater number of code smells can make the software system hard to maintain. Code smell indicates the problems which can reduce the software quality. It is the area within the source code which needs refinement. Code smells presence may lead to overpriced maintenance cost. These smell areas are not any kind of errors in the code. By improving that area, the code will qualitatively and quantitively good. If smells will present in the code, it may lead to software defect in coming time. Objective: The paper aims on Predicting Code Smell (Data Class) present in the source code through the application of various deep learning models. Methodology: we have used 5 deep learning classifiers namely Artificial Neural Network, Convolutional Neural Network, Recurrent Neural Network, Long Short-Term Memory and Deep Belief Network. Additionally, we have used 2 ensemble deep learning models as CNN+LSTM+DNN and CNN+RNN for prediction of the code smells. Result: From our experimental observation it was observed that ensemble of CNN, LSTM and DNN is predicting more Data Class Smells as it having more accuracy (88.8%) as compared to other deep learning classifiers. Here we have taken accuracy as a benchmark performance measure.

articleTitle: Advancing Solar Panel Fault Detection: A Comparative Study of Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Solar panels serve as an efficient and sustainable energy source, enabling the widespread adoption of solar power as a clean alternative to conventional fuels. However, defects arising from manufacturing, transportation, or installation can significantly impact their energy output. This study explores deep learning-based techniques for identifying and classifying visual defects in photovoltaic (PV) modules, including cracking, shading, decolorization, and delamination, to enhance fault detection and improve solar panel efficiency. The proposed approach employs a color image dataset. Initially, the images are pre-processed using an Adaptive Median Filter (AMF) and Contrast-Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE). Then, the spatial and frequency domain features are extracted by Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), Texture, Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT), Grey Level Difference Method (GLDM), and Grey Level Co-Occurrence Matrix (GLCM). The extracted features are inserted into various deep learning (DL) models such as Ensemble DCNN, U-Net, Googlenet, Resnet-101, VGG16, and LinkNet. The classification metrics is used to assess the projected model’s performance. The suggested DL models for identifying visual defects on PV modules is implemented on the PYTHON platform. Compared to all existing DL models with available datasets, U-Net and Link-net demonstrated better accuracy of 97.31% and 93.95% respectively than the other models for the training with 10 epochs with learning rate 80%. Compared to existing DL models and datasets, the results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed models.

articleTitle: Sustainable Wildlife Corridor Monitoring and Conservation Using IoT and Random Forest Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Preserving biodiversity and ecological balance depends on wildlife corridors. For conservation efforts to succeed, monitoring these corridors effectively is vital. This study introduces a method for real-time monitoring of wildlife corridor conditions based on the Internet of Things (IoT) and employs a network of actuators and sensors. Various environmental characteristics, including temperature, humidity, plant density, and animal presence, may be continuously monitored using IoT. The Random Forest method, renowned for its ability to handle complicated datasets and execute precise classification tasks, is used to analyze this data. The Random Forest model analyses the information to determine the corridor's general health, track animal migration patterns, and identify trends in the data. This integrated system aims to improve conservation efforts by giving wildlife managers access to accurate and up-to-date information that they can use to make educated decisions. This strategy aims to enhance the efficacy and efficiency of wildlife corridor monitoring and to help preserve biodiversity by using IoT technology and sophisticated machine learning techniques.

articleTitle: Self-Supervised Multi-scale Attention Cross-Fusion Network for Hyperspectral Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Hyperspectral image (HSI) classification has gained considerable attention due to its potential for precisely discriminating ground objects using detailed spectral and spatial features. This paper proposes a self-supervised multiscale attention-guided cross-fusion network for efficient HSI classification. This approach integrates advanced deep learning methodologies, emphasizing multiscale spatial-spectral attention and self-supervised learning mechanisms to capture complex relationships and enhance feature representation within HSIs effectively. The model’s performance was rigorously evaluated on multiple datasets, including Indian Pines (IP) and Salinas (SA) dataset demonstrating significant improvements over benchmark models such as SSRNet, FCFS-SSL, and S3L. The proposed method achieved superior classification metrics, including higher Kappa, overall, and average accuracies, showcasing its capability to extract deep features and adapt to challenging data complexities. While the model outperformed traditional and semi-supervised methods, challenges such as computational complexity and hardware deployment constraints remain, motivating future exploration of lightweight transformer architectures. Overall, the proposed work offers a promising advancement for efficient, accurate, and scalable HSI classification.

articleTitle: Real-Time Traffic Optimization for Urban Traffic Congestion
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Traffic gridlock is a significant issue in urban centers with growing populations. The increased vehicle congestion has severe consequences, including elevated air and noise pollution levels, higher fuel consumption, and increased stress among commuters. These conditions disrupt daily routines and adversely affect economic productivity and public health. Many cities rely on outdated traffic management systems that operate on fixed schedules and lack real-time adaptability, which worsens congestion. As vehicle numbers surge, replacing these conventional systems with more advanced solutions becomes crucial. The proposed approach emphasizes the integration of machine learning algorithms for real-time vehicle detection and traffic analysis. By comparing various machine learning models, this research aims to identify the most effective algorithm for managing urban traffic, enabling a responsive system that adjusts to live traffic conditions. This method offers a promising solution to alleviate gridlock, address community needs, and reduce the environmental and social costs associated with traffic congestion

articleTitle: Hybrid Quantum Computing and Deep Learning Approaches for Enhancing Wireless Communication Security
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: A potential way to improve wireless communication security in the face of increasingly complex cyberthreats is to combine deep learning techniques with hybrid quantum computing. By combining the processing benefits of quantum algorithms with the pattern recognition powers of deep learning, this article tackles the crucial problems of protecting wireless networks, which are vulnerable to eavesdropping, spoofing, and data breaches. The research uses a hybrid framework in which deep learning models like convolutional neural networks (CNNs) identify and stop possible invasions in real time, while quantum key distribution (QKD) guarantees safe data transfer. Simulations and experimental validation in a 5G network environment show that the proposed system has a 40% reduction in latency and a 35% increase in intrusion detection accuracy compared to traditional security methods, like standard encryption techniques and rule-based intrusion detection systems that lack quantum cryptographic mechanisms and advanced AI-driven pattern recognition. The findings demonstrate that integrating quantum and AI-driven methods to build a more robust wireless communication infrastructure is feasible. The study concludes by highlighting the potential of hybrid quantum-AI systems as a critical first step in protecting next-generation networks.

articleTitle: Improving Malware Detection Accuracy in Volatile Memory using Contrastive Learning and CNN-based Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Cyberattack is getting sophisticated with each passing day. Thus, the forensic techniques need to evolve accordingly. While traditional techniques rely on persistent storage, it is unable to catch hold of critical evidences, as these (critical evidences) reside in the volatile memory. In this scenario, the role of analyzing system RAM in Memory Forensics is pivotal, where transient data is captured. This approach offers insight into system states, running processes and malware activity that would otherwise be lost. The aim of this study is to investigate novel methods for improving memory forensics through the use of machine learning-based classification techniques. The proposed method intends to increase the accuracy of forensic analysis, speed up investigations, and automate the detection of malicious patterns by classifying memory artefacts. The study is based on analysis of binary and multi-class AI models for malware detection in memory forensics. Experimental evaluations were conducted using VGG16, Xception, Inception V3, CNN and Contrastive-Malware-CNN-based classifiers on two image-based datasets capable of extending classifications to 25 distinct families or classes. As indicated in the results, the proposed frameworks achieve better performance, with a classification accuracy of 94.7%, compared to the 91.7% accuracy achieved in previously studied model. This research helps development of an effective and efficient memory forensics framework to fight modern malware threats.

articleTitle: Color Image Enhancement Using Rao Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Enhancing visual data, especially color images is essential in the healthcare sector, security sector, and multimedia applications. Unlike gray-scale images, color images provide richer details but pose unique challenges due to the interdependence of RGB channels. Traditional enhancement methods, such as Histogram Equalization (HE), often fall short for color images, resulting in color distortion and uneven improvements. This paper looks into the effectiveness of metaheuristic optimization algorithms in improving color images. In particular, it discusses metaphor-based algorithms, inspired by natural behaviors such as particle swarm optimization (PSO), with metaphor-less algorithms like Rao-1, Rao-2, and Rao-3 that are based solely on mathematical principles. With the help of these algorithms, several color images were enhanced and performance was measured using measures including SSIM, VIF, PSNR and entropy to measure visual clarity, detail retention, and computational efficiency. This study highlights the strengths and weaknesses of both metaphor-based and metaphor-less metaheuristic approaches. The research gives a methodical comparison that throws light on the suitability of these algorithms and emphasizes the significance of optimization methods with a scientific foundation for advancing picture enhancing tasks.

articleTitle: Innovations to Enhance Traffic Prediction and Empowering IoV for Smart Cities
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Predicting traffic flow is important for improving safety and efficiency in IoV systems. Techniques such as traditional models, deep learning, hybrid approaches, graph-based methods, optimization, edge computing, and feature fusion techniques are examined in this study. Hybrid techniques and Edge computing models reached the highest accuracy of 98.5% and 98.06%, respectively, with minimal error MAE: 4.9, RMSE: 9.8. Deep learning and feature fusion performed well. At the same time, traditional ML and optimization methods lagged. Challenges such as computational complexity and data quality persist. Future work should be on lightweight, scalable, and privacy-preserving models using 5G, IoT, and blockchain for smarter transportation networks.

articleTitle: Campus Carpooling: Optimized Ridesharing for Students using Hybrid Ridesharing Algorithm HRA
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: A student-focused carpooling service created to accommodate the unique transportation needs of college students. Other users can select where they wish to be picked up after individuals post their starting locations, available seats, and routes on the website. The service optimizes the matching process between riders and passengers using a machine learning algorithm to guarantee efficient and comfortable transportation arrangements. Dynamic pricing, which varies based on supply and demand, is one of the system’s unique features. It allows users to choose whether to pay for rides or not, based on their preferences. The platform incorporates user registration and verification to maintain security and community trust, and both riders’ and passengers’ profiles include ratings and reviews to create a reliable user base. The machine learning component improves the overall effectiveness of the service by reducing the overall journey time and distance through the use of clustering and optimization techniques. Additional features including ride monitoring, emergency contact information, identification verification, and an integrated payment channel for paid rides are offered to ensure safety. In-app messaging and notifications make it easier for users to communicate. To ensure smooth operations and quick problem-solving, an admin interface is also offered for managing users, rides, and payments. The initiative aims to establish a carpooling system that is economical, efficient, and sustainable for college students in order to encourage environmentally friendly transportation options on campuses.

articleTitle: Blockchain-Based Identity Verification for Financial Inclusion
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) with blockchain offers a transformative approach to enhancing security in financial services. This fusion leverages AI’s data analysis and anomaly detection with blockchain’s transparency and immutability, enabling improved fraud prevention, identity verification, and regulatory compliance. AI-driven tools can detect suspicious activities in real time, bolstering transaction security while blockchain ensures an unalterable, traceable record. Combining AI-powered biometric authentication with blockchain identity management enhances security and simplifies customer onboarding. Smart contracts further automate and secure transaction processes, reducing risks and minimizing the need for intermediaries. Together, AI and blockchain provide financial institutions with a robust framework for security, transparency, and efficiency in digital transactions, creating a safer, more reliable financial ecosystem.

articleTitle: Enhancing Supply Chain Transparency and Integrity: A Permissioned Blockchain Framework
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Traditional international trade practices have often been plagued by opaque information flows, impeding traceability, and complicating seamless trade operations. Although blockchain technology has emerged as a potential solution for the supply chain and logistics sector, the existing literature predominantly addresses isolated issues such as asset monitoring and traceability, overlooking critical factors such as data integrity and access. This paper proposes a comprehensive blockchain-acquired framework designed to secure supply chain and logistics operations by integrating relevant processes and functions. Through a detailed case study, we demonstrate the effectiveness of the framework in addressing significant vulnerabilities within current supply chain systems. Our findings reveal that the proposed framework not only enhances traceability, but also fortifies data integrity and access controls, thus mitigating critical loopholes that have hindered operational efficiency. Furthermore, we outline several avenues for future research, emphasizing the need for continued exploration of blockchain applications in supply chain management. This work aims to contribute to the development of more transparent, efficient, and reliable trade practices in the global marketplace.

articleTitle: Innovating Healthcare by Unleashing the Power of Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: The proper diagnosis of medical ailments is essential for improving timely and cost-effective patient care. Healthcare professionals rely on scans and patient information to gather accurate details about diseases. In this concern, the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), and Deep Learning (DL) plays an important role in improving patient care and developing an intelligent healthcare system. In the past decade, the utilization of various ML and DL techniques has been recognized as an effective tool for investigating huge amounts of health-related data. Moreover, the advancement of DL has addressed challenges in accuracy and robustness and also promoted the development of reliable diagnostic systems. This article presents a comprehensive survey of various diseases such as Alzheimer's, cancer, diabetes, heart disease, skin disorders, and liver diseases. Thus, the essential aim of the research is to identify the current problems and challenges and to define further directions for the study.

articleTitle: Analysis of Key Parameters in Software Defined Network for Optimizing the Performance
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: SDN is a novel approach to networking by decoupling the control and data planes and allowing for centralized management and dynamic configuration. The paper looks into the core performance parameters critical to SDN functionality, focusing on their role in ensuring efficient, scalable, and reliable network operations. Additionally, it highlights optimization strategies and tools that address the challenges posed by these parameters. This research study aims to provide the desired broad perspective in development of innovative solutions to improve SDN performance in meeting the requirements of modern and emerging networking environments.

articleTitle: Hyperparameter Tuning Of Machine Learning Models: Analysing Student’s Depression Data
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: This research focuses on the tuning of the hyper-parameters of some of the selected machine learning models. Tuning the correct hyper-parameter will use three types of searching techniques for the search space of hyperparameters. The dataset has 502 instances and 11 attributes (1 target attribute). It is a balanced dataset. The target attribute is "Depression" (Yes/No). Our objective is to compare the performance of 10 different supervised machine learning classifiers including Random Forest, KNN, SVM, Logistic Regression, Decision Tree Classifier, Naive Bayes, Gradient Boosting Machine, AdaBoost, Feed Forward Neural Network (MLP) and Extra Trees. Once the comparison report is achieved, we select four different classifiers (KNN, SVM, Logistic Regression and Ada-Boost Classifier), create search space of the hyper-parameters for each classifier algorithm. Every search space is then cross validated through split tests, for three different searching algorithm (grid Search CV, random search CV, Bayesin Optimization) to achieve the maximum accuracy and the perfect fit hyper-parameters for the four classifiers. Provided these classifiers are more generalized and less prone to overfitting. There will be visualization charts in the research for visualizing the improving accuracy for each split test.

articleTitle: Towards a Sustainable Future: Blockchain in Carbon Emission Tracking and Reduction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: This paper explores the potential of blockchain technology in tracking and reducing carbon footprints, contributing to a sustainable future. Traditional methods of monitoring carbon emissions often struggle with inefficiency and lack of transparency. Blockchain’s decentralized and immutable nature offers significant advantages, including enhanced data accuracy and real-time tracking of carbon data. This study reviews existing literature, presents case studies, and analyzes the impact of blockchain applications on carbon footprint management. It also discusses the challenges of implementing blockchain technology and suggests future directions for research and development in this field.

articleTitle: Development and Implementation of Advanced Text Autocorrection via Probabilistic Methods Using Levenshtein Distance and Jaccard Similarity
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: The paper aims at creating an advanced autocorrection system specifically for the Nepali language. This system uses sophisticated natural language processing (NLP) techniques to automatically rectify typographical errors of Nepali texts. The autocorrection system suggests the most likely corrections for misspelt words using the Levenshtein Distance and Jaccard Similarity algorithms. This paper aims to improve the efficiency and user experience across a variety of text-based applications, such as social media, document editing, and messaging, by decreasing the amount of time needed for text editing and increasing text accuracy. The groundwork for future developments in NLP applications for the Nepali language is laid by this effort.

articleTitle: Channel-wise attention based binarization for CNN Architectures
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Attention mechanisms are known to effectively increase the performance of a model by focusing on specific sections of the input while executing a task. Squeeze and Excitation module (SE-Net) and Efficient channel attention module (ECA-Net) are well-known Channel Attention networks that only involve a few parameters to achieve a clear performance gain. In order to further improve the model’s accuracy, Binarized Neural Networks (BNNs) can be introduced in the same. BNNs are deep learning models that use binarized values for activation functions and training weights, instead of fully precised values that leads to much faster computation, occupying less memory and power. Motivated by this, a method of binarization of the convolutional network is proposed in this paper that can enhance the overall model accuracy. In our work, we focused on evaluating the performance of our binarized attention module over the pre-existing ones. Thus, the objective of this work is to design, implement, and evaluate efficient neural network models that balance accuracy and computational efficiency for image classification tasks on datasets with differing complexity levels, such as CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100. By exploring various backbone architectures (e.g., MobileNetV2 and ResNet50), attention mechanisms (e.g., ECANet and SENet), and binarization techniques, this study aims to understand the impact of these components on model performance and resource requirements. Ultimately, the goal is to develop optimized models that achieve high accuracy with minimal computational overhead, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments.

articleTitle: Seasonal crop recommendation using Ensemble classification algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: In today's agricultural landscape, farmers frequently require crop suggestions to make informed decisions. Traditionally, they rely on agriculture officers for such assistance. However, to extend the help to farmers many researchers applied different machine learning techniques to crop and weather datasets. So, an integration of different technologies to analyze the historical soil-crop dataset, and weather details to provide a decision support system to farmers is essential. The primary object of the research work is to guide inexperienced farmers through more accurate crop recommendations. The implementation of different classification algorithms and ensemble approaches leads to improved accuracy in predictions. Ultimately, this empowers farmers to make informed decisions on crop selection.The data collected from http://data.icrisat.org/dld/src/crops.html contains the details of different crops in India along with their geographical locations. The dataset contains crop type, area name, rate of production per hectare, and season. Also, a dataset was collected from the local agriculture office of three districts of Odisha, India for analysis. An approach of analyzing the dataset using five different machine learning algorithms and ensemble methods shall be applied. An android application is developed that analyzes the crop data along with the given location. A model has been proposed to implement a Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Logistic Regression (LR), Decision Tree (DT), and Voting Classifier (VTC) on the cloud dataset. It shows that the Voting Classifier predicts the suitable crops with a higher accuracy of 93%. Overall, the crop recommendation model proposed is driven by the analysis of the cloud crop dataset using machine learning algorithms.

articleTitle: Optimised Firefly Algorithm for Adaptive Band and Feature Selection in HyperSpectral Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: This paper introduces an optimized approach for hyperspectral image classification through Adaptive Band and Feature Selection, utilizing an Improved Firefly Algorithm (IFA). By choosing an ideal selection of spectral bands, the suggested IFA successfully lowers the dimensionality and complexity of the classification task. based on objective functions that maximize divisions between class, such as the Jeffreys–Matusita (JM) distance, eliminating the need for an embedded classifier within the selection process. Additionally, the IFA is applied for feature selection, identifying the most discriminative features from a combination of filter-based feature sets. The method is tested on the Indian Pines hyperspectral image dataset, acquired by AVIRIS sensors. Experimental results demonstrate that the IFA significantly outperforms traditional methods, including the standard Firefly Algorithm, PSO, and PCA, as to classification accuracy and computational efficiency. A MSVM is used to evaluate the classification performance of the selected bands and features, further showcasing the potency of the proposed approach in hyperspectral image classification. This version integrates the results and comparisons with other methods while maintaining clarity and conciseness.

articleTitle: Self-Driving Cars: An Epitome of Technological Innovation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Autonomous vehicles (AVs) are bringing a massive revolution in leveraging advancements in the fields of sensor technologies, artificial intelligence and machine learning algorithms. This paper focuses on providing extensive details on technical foundations, ethical concerns, legal challenges, and societal implications. Key technologies including perception systems, decisionmaking algorithms and experimental frameworks are analysed to understand their role in enabling safe and efficient autonomy. Global regulatory discrepancies, privacy problems, and ethical quandaries in accident scenarios are also examined. The difficulties experienced by systems such as Waymo’s autonomous taxis and Tesla’s Full-Self Driving Beta are demonstrated by real-world case studies. The results highlight the significance of filling key research gaps in the areas of societal repercussions, legal uniformity, and scalability. The future of autonomous vehicles is expected to be inclusive, safe, and morally upright through the promotion of interdisciplinary cooperation. It also considers the economic implications of widespread AV adoption and particularly the impact on employment and infrastructure transformation when making efforts to address these challenges. Exploration of the integration of AVs in existing urban structure which has emphasized the need for adaptive traffic management and energy-efficient solutions have also been done. Trust and acceptance must also be built by raising public awareness and educating about the capabilities and limitations of AVs.

articleTitle: Efficient Task Scheduling for Cloud Environments with MSA: Enhancing Makespan and Resource Utilization
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: People still want the fastest and most effective answers, even as technology improves. Since the advent of cloud computing and its multiple substructures, many algorithms have been proposed to improve the presentation of each unit or structure. The massive cloud can solve any user-supplied task. Therefore, new methods are proposed to improve the process and reduce evaluation time. The task scheduler allocates jobs to virtual machines to maximize efficiency and minimize execution time in cloud computing. This paper introduces the Mantis Search Algorithm (MSA) as a scheduling solution and tests and compares it to other algorithms based on efficiency, makespan, and cost limits. Sexual cannibalism, prey pursuit, and prey assault comprised this optimization process. A multiobjective fitness purpose is created in the CC stage by reducing makespan and optimising resource utilization. There are several ways to test the strategy and evaluate the results. Simulations showed that the MSA technique outperformed alternatives in numerous situations.

articleTitle: Innovative AI Solutions with Animal Detection for Road Safety and Preventing Wildlife Collisions
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Wildlife-vehicle collisions (WVCs) are emerging as a serious concern for road safety. Advanced technologies, such as AI algorithms, IoV frameworks, and multi-sensor systems, provide promising solutions to these situations by detecting animals and alerting drivers. We studied a wide variety of techniques, such as CNNs, YOLO algorithms, and other real-time animal detection frameworks. This paper compares in depth the strengths and limitations of the current solutions in terms of accuracy, speed, and adaptability to different environmental conditions. This paper outlines the opportunities for research in enhancing detection accuracy, reducing false positives, and enabling large-scale implementation through IoV frameworks. This study can foster future interdisciplinary innovation.

articleTitle: Detection of Malicious and Abnormal Users for Policy Enforcement in a Zero Trust Network
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: The zero-trust security model is based on the philosophy of distrust and performs strict identity verification for every user/device attempting to access the system resources. It maintains strict access control and grants the least access privilege to minimize the risk of unauthorized access and data breaches. Users authorized to access any resource in a zero-trust system, are subjected to continuous verification. Although continuous monitoring is crucial for zero-trust systems, there is no literature on its implementation. In this paper, we show that the policy-enforcement-point (PEP) of a zero-trust system could be integrated with an intrusion detection system like Snort to help it with continuous monitoring tasks. Snort is an open-source tool that can capture and log the IP addresses of both the source and destination in any data packet in the network traffic. By packet inspection and analysis, Snort can detect malicious and suspicious activities. We have demonstrated how appropriate Snort alerts can be generated and integrated with a PEP to identify malicious and abnormal users for policy enforcement in a zero-trust system.

articleTitle: Evaluating Deep Learning Models for Brain Tumor Detection Utilizing Transfer Learning and Fine-Tuning Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Brain tumor identification is a significant task in medical imaging, necessitating precise and fast diagnostic methods to enhance patient outcomes. Despite advances in medical imaging technologies, prompt and precise diagnosis of brain tumors remains a face-off. Specifically, Deep Learning networks that make utilization of transfer learning and fine-tuning have demonstrated that they have the potential to be effective in resolving this issue. This investigation compares the performance of some prevalent progressive Deep Learning networks for brain tumor diagnostics, using Transfer Learning and Fine-Tuning approaches. Ten Deep Learning models namely Inception, Xception, ResNet-50, VGG-16, DenseNet-121, ResNet-152, DenseNet-169, VGG-19, EfficientNetB0, and MobileNetV2 are used for performance evaluation in the 4-class classification of brain tumor images. To improve detection capabilities, the models are pre-trained on a huge ‘ImageNet’ database and then fine-tuned using an annotated brain tumor image dataset. The assessment demonstrates that VGG-16 surpasses others with an accuracy of 99.24% for the 4-class classification of brain tumor data.

articleTitle: Optimizing Deep Learning Models through Spatial Attentive Architectural Enhancements and Binarization Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Attention mechanisms in vision applications of the computer world dynamically adjust feature weights to amplify the model’s capability to perceive information. This adaptive recalibration improves the overall effectiveness of the model. Spatial attention has seen widespread use to boost the efficiency of convolutional neural networks by enhancing their ability to model spatial information. This approach significantly improves CNNs’ spatial representation capabilities. Along this line of research, a novel binarized-attention module is drafted by taking spatial attention into consideration. Binary neural networks, which significantly reduce storage and computational requirements, are a promising approach for deploying deep models on resource-constrained devices. This technique offers efficiency in scenarios with limited resources. In this paper, we hereby implemented our algorithm of binarizing the spatial attention module and obtained diverse findings, demonstrating significant improvements in accuracies with fewer classes and degradation of accuracies with higher classes. Various experimental findings reveal that our technique delivers better accuracy with dataset having 10 classes but low accuracy with the one having 100 classes. Additionally, architectural optimizations, including the adoption of deeper networks like ResNet50, contribute to better handling of complex data patterns. While binarization offers computational efficiency, it often results in a trade-off with accuracy. However, selective binarization of specific network layers can mitigate this issue, maintaining a balance between performance and resource utilization. This study provides insights into the synergistic effects of these techniques, offering a pathway for developing efficient and accurate deep learning models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments.

articleTitle: Edge Node Load Balancing Using Game Theoretic Approaches
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: This paper explores the application of game theoretic approaches to load balancing across edge nodes within distributed computing systems. Focusing on a non-cooperative game model, we aim to enhance system efficiency by strategically optimizing resource allocation and load distribution among autonomous edge nodes. Initial simulations demonstrate that our approach not only addresses the inherent complexities of edge environments but also outperforms traditional load balancing mechanisms in terms of both operational efficiency and system responsiveness.

articleTitle: Hybrid Deepfake Detection System: Leveraging AlexNet and LSTM Networks for Enhanced Video Authentication
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: The rapid proliferation of deepfake technology has presented significant challenges in ensuring the authenticity of digital media, posing security risks in various domains, including social media, politics, and corporate communications. This paper proposes a hybrid deepfake detection system that integrates AlexNet, a powerful convolutional neural network (CNN), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to enhance video authentication. The proposed system lever-ages AlexNet's strong capabilities in feature extraction to analyze spatial features within video frames, while LSTM networks process temporal sequences, capturing the dependencies across frames in video streams. By combining these models, our approach delivers an effective deepfake detection system that is robust to subtle manipulations and capable of identifying deepfakes with high precision. Experiments were conducted on publicly available datasets to evaluate the performance of the hybrid model against standalone models and other baseline approaches. The results indicate significant improvements in detection accuracy, with the hybrid system achieving a higher recall and precision rate compared to traditional CNN and RNN-based methods. Furthermore, the proposed system demonstrated resilience against a wide range of deepfake techniques, including facial reenactment and voice synchronization. This work highlights the importance of combining spatial and temporal analysis for reliable video authentication, paving the way for advanced deepfake mitigation strategies in both public and private sectors. The integration of AlexNet and LSTM networks offers a scalable solution for real-time video analysis, providing critical support in com-bating the spread of disinformation and enhancing trust in digital media.

articleTitle: Spatial Domain Image Watermarking Framework using Pixel-Based Saliency Map and Histogram Equalization
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Nowadays, Processing and transmitting data primarily occur in the digital world, making copyright protection a serious concern, especially in data augmentation or reproduction. Digital watermarking is a common solution. This method employs a pixel-based saliency map, histogram equalization, and alpha blending to create a spatial domain watermarking strategy. The saliency map identifies less visible areas in images, embedding information gradually based on histogram data. Alterations outside visually prominent regions remain less noticeable. The histogram approach helps locate areas suitable for concealing confidential information. Experimental results and analysis using various frameworks demonstrate that our method ensures transparency within the cover object while enhancing resilience and concealment capabilities.

articleTitle: Predicting Protein Properties: An Approach Based on Regression for Structure and Function Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Context: Proteins are large and major molecules that are present in all living organisms. They are painted of long chains of amino acids which are connected through peptide bonds. In the post-genomic era protein’s function prediction is much more difficult task. The proteins which are newly spotted has been gradually increasing with the benefit of high-throughput technique. Objectives: The main objective of this research is to predict protein’s function and structure using regression approaches. The other aim is to traverse recent advancements in ML techniques that have greatly enhanced regression-based methods for Predicting proteins properties Method and materials: We used various machine learning algorithms to predict the protein shape, structure and action mechanism. We applied different regressor algorithms such as decision tree regression, linear regression, gradient boosting regression and random forest regression using advanced frameworks such as Scikit-Learn and Tensor Flow. Result: The random forest model shows the best performance across most of the metrics. For MSE both random forest and polynomial regression have the lowest value (0.038). In terms of RMSE, the random forest model has the lowest value (0.194), indicating the smallest average magnitude of errors. The Random Forest model also has the lowest MAE (0.155), reflecting the smallest average absolute errors. Moreover, the random forest model achieves the highest R-Squared value (0.523), explaining the highest proportion of variance in the dependent variable.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: Advanced Deep Learning Framework for MRI Brain Tumor Detection: ResNet50 and GAN-Driven Data Augmentation for Rare Tumor Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: This comprehensive paper combines advanced image processing and deep learning techniques for brain tumor detection and classification in MRI images. Beginning with robust preprocessing methods to extract relevant brain regions, the project employs a ResNet50-based Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for initial classification. Furthermore, it introduces a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) for effective data augmentation, creating synthetic images to enhance model performance. The approach extends to the identification of rare tumor cases, including irregular tumors, enhanced patterns, calcifications, cystic components, and those with hemorrhage or necrosis. The proposed CNN model achieves a test accuracy of approximately 90% after training with augmented data. The project provides a holistic framework for accurate brain tumor detection, leveraging a diverse set of image processing and machine learning methodologies.

articleTitle: AI-driven Student Task Management Platform With Plagiarism Checker For Submissions
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: In current society, plagiarism of material from external sources is common and claiming it as one’s own is considered a serious offense, particularly in academic settings. Plagiarism has become a significant issue among students at all levels-undergraduate, postgraduate and even doctoral. This paper addresses the specific challenge of plagiarism in computer programming assignments, where students frequently blend and modify original solutions to produce fraudulent work. To address this issue, a system has been proposed that enables teachers to efficiently check for plagiarism with a single click by uploading a folder of submissions. Although various software tools have been developed to detect plagiarism, there has been limited evaluation of their effectiveness in accurately identifying the true authorship of submitted work. Our approach leverages artificial intelligence algorithms to break down submitted articles into smaller sections and compare them against existing databases. This research aims to effectively identify and recognize instances of plagiarism while preventing potential copyright issues. Index Terms—Plagiarism detection, Text similarity, Machine learning, Cosine similarity, Semantic analysis

articleTitle: Intelligent Eye Strain Relief Glasses using IoT and Naive Bayes Solutions for Digital Wellness
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Eye strain and its effects on general health have become more pressing issues due to the pervasive nature of digital devices in modern life. This work offers a new approach by combining the Internet of Things (IoT) with Naive Bayes classification for smart eyewear that reduces eye strain. The proposed system aims to reduce digital eye strain by adapting the lens's characteristics in real-time to user behavior and ambient factors. Using the IoT architecture, data like screen time, distance from the device, and ambient lighting conditions may be captured in real-time when users interact with digital displays. Using Naive Bayes classification, this data is processed to identify probable causes of eye strain and suggest suitable eyewear changes to reduce pain. The proposed system provides a preventative method of fostering digital well-being using software and hardware components, such as sensors, microcontrollers, and machine learning algorithms. These smart glasses provide hope for a future free of the negative impacts of digital device use on eye health by making personal recommendations based on each user's unique requirements.

articleTitle: Optimizing Pumpkin Seed Variety Classification: A Logistic Regression Approach to Morphological Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: This paper employs logistic regression to categorise pumpkin seeds into Urgup_Sivrisi and Cercevelik based on a sample morphological database of 2500 pumpkin seeds from Urgup and Karacaoren, Turkey. These features, which are important for seed classification, have been obtained through the use of gray and binary thresholding techniques of the acquired dataset on size, shape and other physical attributes. A binary, logistic regression procedure yielded 86% mean accuracy from 10-fold cross-validation test to prove effective classification between the two seed types. In the classification report, it presented a good equilibrium in the model’s performance. In class ‘0’ (Urgup_Sivrisi) precision was 82%, recall was 93%, and thus F1 score of 0.87 was obtained which very good in terms of detection. In class ‘1’ (Cercevelik), we had a precision of 91% and recall of 78% and the F1-score of 0.84. The macro-averaged F1 was 0.85 while for weight averages of precision, recollect and F1 this was 0.86, indicating same performance of the tool for the two classes. However, depending on the current outcome, it has an acceptable recall overall but more refined recall could be attained from ‘class 1’ to detect other instances of this category. This work shows that the application of logistic regression in agricultural sector can be practical to sort seeds identifying their quality very speedily and accurately. Challenging future works can further investigate more advanced machine learning algorithms and improved features selection to improve the model precision and practicality in seed processing as well as in agricultural activities.

articleTitle: Quantum Task Allocation and Scheduling with Security Enhancements via Quantum Key Distribution
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: As quantum computing progresses, the need for optimized task allocation and scheduling becomes paramount to efficiently harness quantum resources. Simultaneously, ensuring the security of communications in quantum systems is critical, given their vulnerability to quantum-specific attacks. This paper introduces a framework for quantum task allocation and scheduling, augmented with security enhancements using Quantum Key Distribution (QKD). By incorporating novel quantum scheduling algorithms and cryptographic protections, this mechanism offers both high efficiency and strong security. Analytical formulations and simulations confirm the robustness of our approach, demonstrating improvements in both scheduling efficiency and secure communication.

articleTitle: An Integrated Deep Learning Model for Pancreatic Cancer Segmentation and Classification based on CT Images
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Early and accurate diagnosis is needed for successful treatment of pancreatic cancer, as survival rates are low. Computed tomography (CT) is a commonly used diagnostic and staging tool for pancreatic cancers. The difficult task for clinicians and research is that exact segmentation and classification through medical images. On the other hand, manually segmenting volumetric CT scans is a laborious and subjective procedure. Recently the U-Net technique has demonstrated remarkable step in semantic segmentation on medical images. The crucial part is that to differentiate the tumour and non-tumour pancreatic tissues in CT images is the classification of pancreatic cancer. There have been various deep learning models put out. This study presents a unified deep learning model that can accurately partition and classify pancreatic cancer. The U-Net model was trained on annotated CT scans to precisely segment the pancreas and potential lesions, achieving accuracy 99.4%. The DenseNet-121 classifier was subsequently applied to the segmented regions to differentiate tumor and non-tumor tissue. The classification model achieved an accuracy of 99.5%. The aim of this model is to implement a dependable and precise diagnostic system that improves the performance of pancreatic cancer diagnosis.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Deep Learning Framework for Human Activity Recognition using Video Data
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: This research presents a dual-pathway SlowFast network in order to provide a novel approach for the recognition of human actions. The method has the ability to capture low-intensity as well as high-intensity activities efficiently. The model is trained on two different datasets: one on the routine activities, such as sitting and walking, and the other on complex sports and leisure activities. The SlowFast network increases the accuracy in a wide variety of scenarios by incorporating high-level spatial context along with fast motion characteristics using a dual-path architecture. The proposed model outperforms the conventional HAR methods on different grounds such as adaptability and accuracy, and thus aptly useful for applications such as security surveillance, healthcare, and sports analysis. This approach brings forth a robust system able to identify a range of human actions in static as well as dynamic environments by removing some of the limitations from existing HAR models.

articleTitle: Perception Ranking of Buyer's Preference Towards hatchback car-using Multi Criteria Decision Making Technique
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Increased use of internet, social media and technology with availability of range of designs/models of premium hatchback cars offered by reputed brands in this competitive market is a great challenge before the buyers to choose the best one which satisfy his/her requirements. This study employs the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP), robust multicriteria decision making method, to establish the relative significance of factors impacting consumer’s preferences in selection of a car. This study assesses the usability value of the Premium Hatchback Car through user preferences utilizing the AHP method of Multi-Criteria-Decision-Making techniques. The usability value allows for the ranking of parameters/features based on user’s perceptions, aiding them in choosing the most optimal option as per the buyer’s preference. The AHP technique facilitates the computation of usability value by employing a hierarchical approach to establish criteria and a performance evaluation process to rate and rank parameters. This enables the provision of optimal recommendations to consumers when purchasing a car with superior usability value.

articleTitle: Building Aether Sensor Network using LoRaWAN Network
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: The Aether sensor network is a system of sensors that are used to monitor the environment and detect changes in the atmosphere. It is a system of sensors that are used to monitor the environment and detect changes in the atmosphere. The Aether sensor network is connected to an IoT platform, which enables it to be deployed globally and collect data on a variety of environmental phenomena. One such phenomenon is measuring air quality by detecting pollutants, toxins, allergens, and particulate matter. In this research, the authors develop an Aether Sensor Network using the LoRaWAN network.

articleTitle: Sentiment analysis using machine learning techniques with a digital dataset survey
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: The applications of sentiment analysis are diverse and impactful for society. This research paper presents a comprehensive study on sentiment analysis using machine learning algorithms to interpret emotions and opinions expressed in text data. The study focuses on various contexts, including product reviews, social media posts, and news articles, to extract meaningful insights that inform decision-making processes. The paper discusses the challenges of sentiment analysis, such as handling noisy data, language nuances, and sentiment classification accuracy, and emphasizes the importance of advanced techniques to capture the complexity of human emotions. The study also highlights the number of digital datasets available for sentiment analysis that may be taken from various product reviews and social media platform comments.

articleTitle: FRANN: Fuzzy Rough Set Based Artificial Neural Network for Prediction of Rainfall Status
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Rainfall status prediction is a process of forecasting the future status or condition of rainfall for a particular region. Prediction of rainfall status is essential because heavy or low rainfall may have many adverse effects on agriculture, transportation, environment, living conditions and economic strength. So, accurate prediction of rainfall status is helpful in designing better action plans for water resource management, disaster risk reduction, sustainable development, emergency management and improving living conditions. Computational intelligence and approximate reasoning of conventional machine learning models are limited by incomplete or imperfect knowledge. However, the soft computing techniques have the capabilities to handle uncertainty, imprecision, partial truth and approximate reasoning to extract information in a number of ambiguous situations. In this aspect, a fuzzy rough set (FRST) based artificial neural network (ANN) model is proposed to predict the future rainfall status. Incorporating FRST method in ANN model can improve the prediction accuracy and reduce the overheads associated with both memory as well as computation time by selecting the dominant attributes and handling inconsistent data present in the information system. Rainfall status prediction accuracy of the proposed hybrid model is compared with two other hybrid models namely FRST based decision tree (DCST), FRST based support vector machine (SVM) and three other existing classification based prediction models namely DCST, SVM and ANN. The findings of the result suggest that the proposed model outperform its counterparts.

articleTitle: AI Powered Smart Recognition of Plant Diseases with Vernacular Language Support
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: The agricultural sector has faced quite a few problems in which high-end knowledge and technologies cannot be easily accessed. Among those problems, yield, showing the farmer’s livelihood, is also badly affected. Therefore, the management of these plant diseases is one of the greatest concerns. Agri Insight is the new generation of chatbots developed for Tamil-speaking farmers through multimodal machine learning and advanced AI. This AI technology ensures real-time and accurate diagnosis of plant diseases based on audio, text, and images. The written symptom reports of the plants are interpreted by Natural Language Processing models. Convolutional Neural Networks also interpret the visual signals of the illnesses of the plants through photographs. Besides, the speech recognition of audio inputs further enhances the diagnostic capability of the chatbot. This incorporates all of these input types into the system to enhance the accuracy of prediction and reduce false diagnoses. The chatbot, apart from identifying diseases, suggests treatments and preventive measures specific to the Tamil agricultural scenario. The integration of accurate real-time plant disease diagnosis using input from text, voice, and images increases accessibility and resilience. The system uses a constantly updated knowledge base on seasonal variations, new diseases, and agricultural methods specific to the location. Agri Insight is a real-time support system accessible to Tamil-speaking farmers with an aim to boost crop protection, increase production, and reduce crop loss. The multilingual and multimodal capabilities of the chatbot are extremely useful in the rural areas while promoting sustainable agricultural practices and the standard of living of farmers. The model results have been remarkably good with accuracy at 98.43%, precision at 96.78%, and recall at 95.60%.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis and Early Detection of Lung Cancer with Spiking Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Cancer of the lung occurs when non-native lung cells grow uncontrollably. The increased incidence of this disease has raised both sexes mortality rates. Lung cancer is a disease that cannot be eradicated, although its risk can be diminished. The survival rate of lung cancer is greatly affected by its early identification. Training the model, extracting features, binarizing, decreasing noise, and converting to grayscale are suggested steps. We convert RGB photographs to grayscale first. Noise reduction removes background noise. A threshold value binarizes grayscale pictures into binary. Feature extraction uses directional gradient histograms, the Gabor filter, and standard deviation. Training the model with the Spiking Neural Network (SNN) ensures accuracy and durability. Compared to Alex Net and CNN, the suggested model is more accurate. It greatly increases lung cancer detection with 91.14% accuracy. This emphasizes early detection's role in lung cancer survival. The proposed method combines state-of-the-art feature extraction with model training to diagnose lung cancer accurately. Due to its precision, this approach may improve diagnostics and health outcomes.

articleTitle: Optimizing Human Sleep Patterns Using AI-Driven Insights from Wearable Data and Behavioral Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Conventional methods for optimizing sleep, such as sleep diaries and questionnaires, frequently depend on subjective data that is vulnerable to variation and personal preference. These techniques fall short of offering precise and useful insights for individualized sleep enhancements. In contrast, this study collected wearable data from 50 participants over a 30-day period, and the analysis was driven by AI to uncover insights and provide personalized recommendations. The method examined physical activity, heart rate variability, and sleep stages using sophisticated machine learning models, particularly Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. The association between environmental conditions and individual sleep behavior over time revealed a 12% reduction in nighttime disturbances and a 20% increase in deep sleep duration. The suggested approach outperforms conventional methods by providing unbiased, data-driven therapies customized to the unique sleep habits of each person. The AI-driven system showed a considerable improvement in sleep quality through focused interventions, making it a superior alternative for optimizing sleep compared to conventional approaches that lack accuracy and customization.

articleTitle: Intelligent Legal and Technical Strategies to Mitigate Cybersquatting: Bridging Global Frameworks and Indian Contexts
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Cybersquatting, the unauthorized registration of domain names mimicking established trademarks, threatens online identity management and intellectual property rights. This study examines the legal and regulatory frameworks addressing cybersquatting, focusing on India’s reliance on the Trade Marks Act, 1999, and the IT Act, 2000, in contrast with international policies like UDRP and ACPA. Through case studies and statistical insights, it identifies legislative gaps in India and proposes actionable reforms to enhance protections, promote ethical digital practices, and foster a secure online ecosystem.

articleTitle: Energy Consumption Optimization using Big Data Analytics for Smart Grid Management
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: The application of big data analytics to improve energy usage efficiency in smart grids has been prompted by the rising need for power management. Adding to the above, it poses a big data solution for demand prediction, load consolidation, and fault diagnosis. Establishing the new and state-of-the-art innovative LSTM network that was employed in the forecast yielded a higher demand forecast accuracy of 94.2% compared to the previous systems. The load balancing index achieved 92% with an accuracy of 93.7% in fault detection, thus minimizing maintenance cost by 14.7% while improving grid reliability. The proposed model was found to give better results than previous conventional machine learning techniques and even modern ones which are more complex, especially for an ever-changing grid environment. Overall, these findings show the promise of big data solutions for handling the challenges of the contemporary smart grid while improving its efficiency through energy optimization. Consequently, this work lays a framework for subsequent studies on the remaining applications of advanced analytics in energy management systems.

articleTitle: Neurodynamic Mapping for Cybersickness Prediction in 3D Game Immersion
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: The rapid expansion of virtual reality (VR) applications in gaming and training has highlighted cybersickness, a condition marked by symptoms such as nausea, dizziness, and disorientation. Traditional assessment methods often rely on subjective reporting, which hampers timely intervention. This study aims to develop a novel approach for predicting the onset of cybersickness through neurodynamic mapping of electroencephalogram (EEG) data and heart rate variability (HRV) in immersive 3D VR environments. Spiking neural network (SNN) architecture to analyze integrated EEG and HRV data collected from participants engaged in 3D VR games. Key EEG channels, particularly F7, Cz, and O2, were identified as critical biomarkers for susceptibility to cybersickness. Real-time monitoring of brainwave frequencies (delta, theta, alpha, and beta) enabled tracking of changes associated with symptom onset. SNN model achieved a prediction accuracy of 85.9% at resting baseline conditions and detected cybersickness events with an accuracy of 76.6%. The dynamic characteristics of the identified biomarkers suggest potential for enhancing prediction models over time. This research introduces a groundbreaking method for predicting cybersickness in VR gaming by leveraging neurodynamic mapping and SNNs. Our findings provide insights into the neural mechanisms underlying VR-induced motion sickness and have significant implications for improving user experience across various applications, including gaming and virtual therapy. The integration of neurodynamic feedback systems could foster more immersive and user-friendly VR environments by facilitating timely interventions to mitigate cybersickness.

articleTitle: LBPNET: Detection of Fake Face Currency through LBP-Based Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: The escalating sophistication of counterfeit face currency demands innovative solutions for robust detection. In this study, we propose LBPNET, a novel approach employing Local Binary Pattern (LBP) feature extraction and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to address the challenges posed by realistic fake currencies. LBP descriptors are extracted from currency images, capturing subtle patterns invisible to the human eye. These descriptors serve as inputs for a CNN, named LBPNET, trained to discern genuine from counterfeit face currencies. The model undergoes a comprehensive training phase, incorporating diverse currency images, to establish a generalized and adaptive detection system. In testing, new currency images are evaluated using the trained LBPNET to identify the presence of fake or non-fake currency, showcasing the model's adaptability to emerging counterfeit variations. This approach integrates machine learning and image processing to enhance detection capabilities, offering a promising solution for the evolving landscape of counterfeit face currency across forensic and social media domains.

articleTitle: Enhanced Knowledge Extraction using Cutting-Edge Rough and Soft Graph Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: Addressing uncertainties in data is crucial for real-world applications, including social networks, where relationships often lack clear definition. Soft and rough graph theories allow for nuanced modeling of such data by extending traditional graph structures with parameters that account for uncertainty. Social networks exhibit complex, often ambiguous relationships that traditional graphs cannot fully represent, especially in dynamic, imprecise settings. This study aims to explore soft and rough graphs as effective tools for extracting knowledge from social networks by modeling vague or partially known relationships. Our rough graph analysis identified strong, definite communication channel between employees sharing dual expertise and different weaker channels based on single expertise, suggesting potential collaboration points. In soft graph analysis, two subgroups were detected around shared interests in Sports and Music, identifying central and bridging users within the network. Soft and rough graphs enhance knowledge extraction from social networks, enabling insights into communities, influencers, and communication channels that reflect the uncertain and dynamic nature of social interactions, which can also be used in data science to evaluate ambiguous or incomplete datasets, find hidden patterns, and enhance decision-making in fields like network optimization, fraud detection, and recommendation systems. This approach is shown to be beneficial in structuring and understanding intricate social data patterns.

articleTitle: Modified Grey Wolf Optimization using Refraction Learning and Differential Evolution Mutation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Systems and Intelligent Computing (ESIC)
abstract: An enhanced variant of the Grey Wolf Optimisation (GWO) technique is presented in this paper, addressing a number of issues, including reduced population diversity, slow convergence and vulnerability to local optima. The proposed variant incorporates innovative techniques, including Opposition Learning, Refraction Learning (RL), Differential Evolution Mutation and a non-linear time-varying hyperparameter tuning mechanism. Combining these strategies greatly enhances the standard GWO’s performance, leading to a more streamlined and effective search procedure. This enhancement leads to better performance in multi-modal landscapes, facilitates escaping local optima and allows the search space to be explored more extensively. Extensive testing across 23 benchmark functions demonstrates that the new variant outperforms the original GWO as well as other contemporary optimization methods. The results indicate substantial improvements in convergence speed, global search capability and solution accuracy, demonstrating how effective this method can be as an optimisation tool for solving challenging real-world issues.
